188	#### Group D — Presence: ingress, TRANSIT, return, dormancy, weld and cut
189	
190	**HE-20. Instance, ingress, TRANSIT, egress and return.** *Rule.* The record has a **home body** (default: derelict B, the web-intrusion side, DA OQ-V5). At TELL entry (observed as `tell_epoch != last_seen_tell_epoch`, the **first evaluation of every record in every run, ahead of dormancy**; transition guard 2), if `body_of(locus_section_id)` is not the record's body, the record leaves its body **whether or not that body is loaded** (E7 `unregister_subject` only if the ref is still registered, because HE-34 already unregistered it when the body unloaded; an egress mark at the old position, inserted into the block-level ring with the old, possibly unloaded, `section_id` and not ageing until that section loads, HE-21; the departed-from body is stored as `from_body_id`), enters `TRANSIT` with `transit_until_T = tell_enter_T + INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS` (the destination body, `transit_to_body_id`, is the locus body), and arrives at a hull segment of the locus body chosen by HE-F9: the compartment **one room hop from the room of the highest-`lux_pm` living seat in the locus body** (none lit or none present: the locus section's outermost compartment; ties lowest room id, then lowest hull-segment id), **never a room holding a living seat and never inside `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` of a living seat that is `linked` to the entry (HE-19)**, no earlier than `INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS` after TELL entry *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. The candidate entries are composed from published Layout reads only: a *hull entry* is an `anchor_geometry` point (section-local, composed with `section_offset`) of a hull-bearing compartment of the locus body that lies within `HULL_CONTACT_PX` of a hull face, paired with the lowest id returned by `hull_segments_near(section_id, anchor_px, HULL_CONTACT_PX)`; there is no `solid_in` sampling and no unpublished room-to-segment read, and the chosen `ingress_seg`, `ingress_anchor_px` and `ingress_mark_T` are persisted (HE-41). The ingress mark (smear and radial hairlines at the segment) is laid `INGRESS_MARK_LEAD_TICKS` before the body appears, so a player looking at that wall sees the arrival coming; on arrival the record registers (E6) and enters STALK (or LURK if the phase is already CALM for a reason other than an abort, for example a return home completing; an abort cancels an outbound arrival instead, see below) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **This departure is the one exemption from HE-21's dormancy** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the default home body is derelict B, which is usually not the body the player is on, so without the exemption a record whose own body is unloaded would be frozen by its own dormancy rule at the first TELL on the home ship or derelict A and a told breach would have no horror in it: cry-wolf, Pillar 1's "the tell is a promise")*. A record already in TRANSIT that sees a new `tell_epoch` retargets: `transit_to_body_id` becomes the new locus body and `transit_until_T` is recomputed from the new TELL entry. **TELL abort while in TRANSIT:** if the phase leaves TELL with an aborted outcome while the record is outbound (it has not yet arrived), the arrival is cancelled, nothing is injected into the player's body, and the record heads back: `transit_to_body_id` becomes `from_body_id` (with `RETURN_HOME` 1 the home body), `transit_leg` becomes RETURN (it is OUTBOUND while heading for a locus body, including after a retarget to a new locus, and RETURN while heading home), `transit_until_T = abort_T + RETURN_DELAY_TICKS`, and the arrival at that body follows HE-21 (it waits if that body is unloaded); an ingress mark already laid stays (it is a true mark) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: an abort must send a restraint signal, not inject a CALM presence into the ship that held its fire)*. If no entry is legal the record stays in TRANSIT and retries each run (diagnostic `horror_ingress_pending`; a BREACH entered with a pending ingress is a cry-wolf defect and an acceptance criterion). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **The rule relaxes so a told breach cannot pass with nothing in it:** at `tell_enter_T + INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS + STALK_VISIBLE_FLOOR_TICKS` (540 at the placeholders) the entry rule falls back to the *nearest legal hull anchor* (HE-F9: the hop-1 and standoff conditions drop out; the entry is the hull entry nearest by room hops to the lit seat's room whose room holds no living seat), whose mark is laid at once and whose body arrives `INGRESS_MARK_LEAD_TICKS` later, no later than `TELL_MIN_TICKS`; only when every hull room holds a living seat does the record stay pending (AC-HE-44). **Return:** when `RETURN_HOME` is 1 (default [PH]), `RETURN_DELAY_TICKS` after SUBSIDING ends or after a TELL abort the record returns to its home body by the same rule (no seat target: the home body's outermost compartment, lowest ids; the legality tests still apply); when `RETURN_HOME` is 0 it does not return and LURKs in the body of the last breach (the creative-director's lean; an Open Question bound to validation target (2), the 70 % CALM sighting: if the target fails, flip this knob first). All choices are deterministic functions of Attention's locus, Emitter reads and ids; nothing is authored (DA:101 "authoring places no entity"). TRANSIT is unregistered, has no position, publishes `state` TRANSIT and `transit_until_T`, harms nothing and lays no marks. The fiction is that the web runs through hulls; both ends leave a mark. Whether a CALM presence aboard the home ship after a home-ship breach is acceptable is settled for MVP in Open Question 6: default `RETURN_HOME` 1, and the departure rule above makes the told breach independent of that knob (with `RETURN_HOME` 0 the record still leaves an unloaded body at every TELL elsewhere, so a TELL is never empty) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *Why.* The first draft's "lowest-id hull segment of the outermost compartment" could place the entity rooms from the player and let it arrive late in BREACH (cry-wolf); one-hop ingress keeps teeth and keeps the approach told. *(orchestrator ruling: ingress refined to one room hop.)* *Cites.* DA:101, AT-12.
191	
192	**HE-21. Dormancy.** *Rule.* A record whose body is unloaded is frozen: no step, no mark ageing, no disturbance, **no fast-forward** (LS-17, LSG:174). **The single exemption is the TELL departure of HE-20** (the new-`tell_epoch` comparison runs before this rule, so an unloaded record whose body is not the locus body leaves for TRANSIT; it does nothing else) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. A mark's `life_left` falls only while the mark's section is loaded (an egress mark laid in an unloaded section is inserted at once and starts ageing when that section loads). A record in TRANSIT whose destination body unloads waits. Answer to Web Map ASK-H1: yes. A record may enter TRANSIT toward an unloaded body (for example a return home to derelict B while it is unloaded). It stays in TRANSIT, unregistered, with no position, no marks and no harm, and arrives at its first run after the body loads with a legal HE-20 entry. The transit machine's `TRANSIT_HOLD` and pod states are Web Map's and are never read as Horror's TRANSIT. *Cites.* LSG:174, LS-17, WM:458.
193	
194	**HE-22. Weld and cut.** *Rule.* The path cache is keyed by the layout (HE-25) and recomputed on any `layout.state` change (a weld or cut applying, MSA-14 / MSA-20). If a weld changes `locus_body` membership, the target body is re-derived from `locus_section_id` on the next run (`locus_body` is recorded at TELL entry and is replaced mid-epoch only by an AT-14 fallback, which TellAudit records as LOCUS_FALLBACK; Horror re-reads `locus_section_id` each run). If a cut removes the section the record stands in from its body, the record's `body_id` is re-derived from `body_of(section_id)`; if its section is gone the record goes to TRANSIT with an egress mark and re-enters its home body. **Re-basing the body-frame points** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: Layout owns the frame, G1/G6; a weld re-bases the absorbed body by `frame_shift_px`, Layout D.6, and the MVP horror's home body, derelict B, is the absorbed body)*: at the start of each run, if `section_offset(section_id)` or `body_of(section_id)` differs from the stored `offset_seen_px` / `body_id` (a weld or cut moved the record's section, Layout LY-16/LY-17), Horror re-bases every persisted body-frame point of the record (`pos_px`, `locked_pt`, `ingress_anchor_px` and any other body-frame px pair in HE-41 groups 1, 3 and 5; section-local fields such as `goal_wp` are untouched) by `delta = section_offset(section_id) − offset_seen_px`, re-derives `body_id` from `body_of(section_id)`, stores the new `offset_seen_px`, and calls E8 `set_subject_anchor(ref, pos_px)` in the same run. The Emitter derives the HORROR subject's `body_id` itself (EM-4, EM-21) and lands the new anchor at the next `emitter.place`. Horror has no cut verb and does not interrupt a cut; Modular Ship Assembly states the same ("Horror and Attention have no cut verb; the breach rhythm uses STRESS and M17, not detaches", MSA-22). *Cites.* MSA-14 / MSA-20 (weld and cut apply), MSA-22 (no cut verb).
195	
196	#### Group E — Movement and pathing
197	
198	**HE-23. Own position, Body's pure step.** *Rule.* Positions are Horror's, in integer base px with a two-axis sub-pixel residue and `last_octant`, inside `horror.state`. Movement calls Body's pure `LocomotionStep` (BDY-10) with `collide` bound to Layout `solid_in`, using Body's foot box (`FOOT_BOX_W` 16, `FOOT_BOX_H` 8, CITED; the 64 to 96 px sprite is visual only, because a larger box could never use an open doorway whose passage extent is exactly 16 across). Per run the horror picks one octant (the integer argmax of the eight unit vectors against the direction to the next waypoint, ties lowest octant) and steps once per tick for the five ticks of the run. There are no `AGENT` rows in Body at MVP (preserving `MAX_ACTORS` 8 headroom for Vertical Slice B seats), no `CharacterBody2D` and no physics query (CR-13 G3, H10). A horror's footprint is a Graph trail or a Horror mark, never a Body fact (BDY-4). `pos_prev` is the position at run start and `pos_curr` the position at run end. -> ADR candidate (1): horror position ownership versus Body `AGENT` rows. *Cites.* BDY-4, BDY-10, BDY-15.
199	
200	**HE-24. Speeds and the escape invariant.** *Rule.* Registered constants, in milli-px per tick: `V_CREEP_MPX` 1000 (LURK, STALK in a TELL, RETREAT, the arrival walk), `V_HUNT_MPX` 1500 (STALK in BREACH). Each tick adds the speed to an accumulator, steps `floor(acc / 1000)` px and keeps the remainder (persisted per record). Registered invariant (HE-F6): `V_CREEP_MPX < V_HUNT_MPX < V_WALK × 1000` (2000), so **a walking seat, including a CRITICAL walk-only seat, always outpaces it**, and there is no lunge travel (the strike resolves at the locked point). A seat that is *carrying* moves at `V_CARRY` 1 (CITED, BDY-13): `V_HUNT_MPX` exceeds it, so a carrier cannot out-walk the approach, and a carrier needs 72 ticks (73 on a diagonal octant) to clear the disc against 40 available (`UNFOLD_LO` 95 less 54 for reaction less 1 for command application; conflict C-HE-8), so **a carrier who does not drop the cargo is struck on 7 of the 18 draws (38.9 %)**: the intended answer is to drop the cargo and walk (Interaction's `drop` is a TAP, lit-exempt and uninterruptible, IA-28; it can only be refused `OBSTRUCTED` when no free cell exists, which is an authoring defect to be lint-covered and a cross-GDD note to Interaction), or accept the hit; the telegraph length is **not** tied to the seat's `V_CARRY` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the 38.9 % figure is now explicit rather than implicit, and the drop is the stated counterplay)*. *(orchestrator ruling: stated as intended; hauling is where the horror bites, Pillar 5 risk; the DA-29 wording note is an owed row.)* Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): 'drop the cargo' is confirmed as the intended price of hauling (a carrier who keeps the cargo is struck on 7 of 18 draws, 38.9 %); `R_SNAP_PX` stays 72 and 48 is the ruled lever (HE-F5, worked example) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *Cites.* DA-29, BDY-13, REG `V_CARRY`.
201	
202	**HE-25. Pathing over Layout reads.** *Rule.* The horror searches an integer room graph built from Layout `room_adjacency(section_id)` over every section of its body (`sections_of`), excluding any edge whose door leaf is closed or **not passable** (a *passable leaf* is open with `open_extent_px` at least the foot-box extent across its wall run, 16 px (`FOOT_BOX_W`) across an E-W wall and 8 px (`FOOT_BOX_H`) across a N-S wall, from Layout's `door_passage` (HE-19); a leaf opened to less is solid to the horror) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Breadth-first by hop count, ties lowest room id, at most `PATH_EXPANSIONS_MAX` node expansions per run (HE-F10); the result is cached as a next-hop table per goal room and layout key. **One graph, one goal rule (the surrogate-goal BFS)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the text had defined the pathing graph two ways, an open-leaf BFS and the full adjacency truncated at a closed leaf)*: the goal room is chosen over the full adjacency (closed and impassable leaves counted for distance, E-HE-20); the search runs on the passable-leaf graph only; when the goal room is not reachable the *surrogate goal* is the reachable room with the smallest full-adjacency hop distance to the goal room (ties lowest room id), and the horror walks there and stops. Inside a room it steers by octant toward the next waypoint (the centre of a door's hinge-aware `gap_rect`, not the sill centre or the leaf, or an `anchor_geometry` point) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; a waypoint is **reached** when the foot point is within `ARRIVE_PX` (8 px [PH], at least the largest per-run displacement, 8 px at `V_HUNT_MPX`, so a run can never step over a waypoint) of it. There is no obstacle avoidance beyond the **local slide rule**, which uses only the persisted `blocked_runs` counter: when the previous run ended `blocked`, `blocked_runs` is 1 and the run uses the adjacent octant (±1) with the larger dot product against the direction to the waypoint (ties lowest octant); at `blocked_runs` 2 it uses the other adjacent octant; from 3 it returns to the direct octant. Authoring contract: a room's walkable floor must let straight octant steps between its sills and anchors succeed with at most this slide (lint `ROOM_NONCONVEX_PATH`, owed to Layout and Derelict Authoring; an L-shaped footprint fixture is AC-HE-128). On a NONE or UNKNOWN Layout read it holds its last waypoint for at most `HOLD_MAX_RUNS` (counted in the persisted `hold_runs`), and then **the fallback depends on the phase: in CALM and TELL it goes to LURK; in BREACH it stays in STALK and holds position (LURK is n/a in BREACH, so a hold-then-LURK there would break the phase view and leave a breach with a horror that cannot do harm); in SUBSIDING it goes to RETREAT**; a record in RETREAT holds in place in any phase *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; **UNKNOWN is never read as "unlit" or as "open"**. If `step` reports no movement for `BLOCKED_RUNS_MAX` consecutive runs it discards the cached hop and re-paths once; if it is still without movement after a second `BLOCKED_RUNS_MAX` runs it is **wedged**, and the defined outcome is RETREAT (counter `horror_wedged`, `cooldown_until_T := T`; in BREACH it then returns to STALK and re-paths, so a wedge repeats visibly in the diagnostics and is an authoring signal, never a silent permanent stall) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Zero `probe()` calls at MVP. `NavigationServer2D` and `NavigationAgent2D` are rejected (node- and server-based, outside the replay hash; H10, G3). `route_length_px` stays diagnostic (LY:310). Layout now states (ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md, LY-28 reads and LY-33) that `layout_hash()` does **not** cover door state and that a reader caching on door geometry keys on `version(section_id)`; the cache key is therefore `(goal_room, layout_hash, version(section_id) of every section of the body)`, a restore (where `version` resets) is an unconditional rebuild, and the Horror-computed closed-leaf hash is retired (C-HE-13 closed 2026-10-27, design review). -> ADR candidate (2). *Cites.* LY:296-310, LY:446, EM:723.
203	
204	**HE-26. Doors and the counterplay set.** *Rule.* A closed door leaf is solid to the horror (Layout `solid_in`). It issues no `set_opening`, opens no door, and may GOUGE or RUPTURE a hull segment, never a door. The **whole MVP counterplay set** is: retreat (walk away: `V_HUNT_MPX < V_WALK × 1000`), close a door (the strike room test and solid leaf; the horror holds at the sill and marks the leaf, below), go dark (the seat leaves target preference on the next run **only if no other light reaches it: a lamp-off seat under a lit fixture or in a Chemlight pool is still lit and still targetable, HE-13** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; its price is every lit-only channelled verb for the breach and the ship under STRESS unattended), pod-hop (the departed seat leaves `locus_body`, so `exogenous_permitted(actor_section(seat))` fails and an in-flight REACH on it fizzles; on a derelict locus, the departure of the last occupant recorded at BREACH entry also ends the breach, AT-12 (iii)), drop the cargo (turns a carrier into a walker) and the **glowstick work-light** (*light the job, not yourself*: a thrown Chemlight lights a workspace so the player can step out of it dark; it does not pull the horror). The suppressant is *not* in the set (HE-39). **A horror may path and stand in derelict A's `a_spine` at the MVP** (Boarding ASK-BS-H1 / OQ-BS-33 answered by the owner) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R21: the option that needs the least new content and preserves user rulings X6 and D63)*: ingress (HE-20) lands at a hull entry one room hop from the lit seat's room and never in a living seat's room, and a stalking horror follows the lit seat through any open door, so a carrier in the 3-wide spine can meet one. No bypass is added and the spine is not widened, because the ruled exits already hold in a single corridor: drop the cargo and walk back the way the carrier came (a walking seat outpaces `V_HUNT_MPX`, HE-24), stillness and darkness, or a door shut behind; this is the intended price of hauling (D63, 7 of 18 draws for a carrier who keeps the cargo, E-HE-27). The existing guards are the dead-end lint (E-HE-26) and the drop's one-free-cell question (Open Question 7); E-HE-59. **The anti-pillar's "tools may repel or distract (flares, torches, decoys)" is deliberately unused at MVP and deferred to Vertical Slice (`repel`, flares, decoys): MVP counterplay is avoidance only, and the routed thread's "tools repel, never kill" is a boundary (no tool ever kills, HE-38) and not an MVP promise that a tool repels.** *(orchestrator ruling: the earlier phrase "glowstick lure" is reworded because HE-13 prefers seats only and a glowstick is not a seat; creative-director concurs; decoys are Vertical Slice.)* No response is free and none is dominant: abort loses the job, hiding loses the task and the ship, going dark loses the lit verbs, committing risks a rung. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2)* **A closed door is a priced, visible refuge** (the creative-director's lean, taken because the user delegated the call). When the target is a lit seat behind a closed or impassable leaf, the horror walks to the surrogate goal (HE-25) and **camps at the sill**: on the run it becomes stationary there (edge-triggered by the persisted `held_at_leaf` flag) it lays one HAIRLINES mark on the leaf face (a true ring entry; no M17 call, no hull damage, no GOUGE, no RUPTURE; counter `horror_leaf_marks`), and it stays while that seat remains the target and the phase is BREACH, recomputing the target every run as ever. The door therefore costs what the rules already price (the task, the ship under STRESS, the lit verbs while dark) and now also shows the player that the thing is waiting on the other side, with the leaf mark as the post-hoc evidence; what it does not do is damage the ship on the player's behalf. The alternatives (an anchor GOUGE fallback; leaving the playtest band as the only price) are recorded in Open Question 33 and not adopted. **A door closed on the horror.** If a leaf closes while the horror's foot box overlaps it (Layout's close-safety counts seats' foot boxes, not the horror's), the next run ejects it as the first step of guard 4: it moves back along `−last_octant` in 8 px increments up to 32 px to the first position for which `solid_in(foot_box)` is false (at most four queries, inside the five-query budget); if none is free it is wedged (RETREAT, `horror_wedged`, HE-25). It never embeds, wedges silently or passes through a leaf; counter `horror_door_ejected`; AC-HE-137. The preferred long-term fix, Layout's close-safety including a published horror foot box (`OBSTRUCTED`), is an ask in Open Question 32 and would make the eject unreachable. *Cites.* AT-12, DA-29, EM:89.
205

257	**HE-42. Determinism.** *Rule.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)* The two draw kernels (Attention's `restore_epoch` key and a Horror-private epoch seed) are replaced by the one below; Attention's AT-8 calls the same function. All simulation randomness is `rng_derive(world_seed, "horror.tell", counter_eff)`, used for the REACH length only, where `counter_eff = threat_counter(counter)` and **`threat_counter(c) = c + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE × restore_epoch` is the kernel's one derivation for threat draws** (the stream-name hash stays cached and unchanged; Attention and Horror call it and neither defines its own). `restore_epoch` is a persisted u32 **owned by Save/Load** (starts at 0), held in the per-slot side file `slot_epoch.bin` (u32 + CRC32, written atomically by temp file and rename by the Save/Load worker); it is in no generation file, so generation bytes and every trailer SHA never change, and each generation header carries only a read-only copy for recovery (R14). A death-stub restore advances it by 1; a Continue of a `QUIT` generation that is the newest non-demoted verified generation carries it unchanged (R13, user ruling D16: not steerable by quit); a Continue of any other generation (after a kill, crash or fallback), in-process or after a fresh process start, advances it. Save/Load writes an advance in a pre-restore staging step and calls `request_restore(gen, restore_epoch)` only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`; on a failed write or after `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (500 ms placeholder) it proceeds with the advanced epoch in memory, logs `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` and sets `save_status = FAILED` (a listed exposure: a kill before a later successful write may replay that epoch once). So two death restores of one autosave give two new epochs, and a Save & Quit then Continue replays the same REACH lengths: quit-and-continue is no reroll oracle *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14; cross-GDD fix)*. The kernel exposes it read-only in `kernel.clock` as `(T, world_seed, restore_epoch)`, sim-visible and pure. `RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE` is 1,048,576 (2^20) and is the kernel's constant (registry request: its source moves from Attention to the kernel, with Attention, Horror and Save/Load in `referenced_by`); the lint `counter < RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE` holds. Horror reads `restore_epoch` through `threat_counter` at the draw and at no other time, never stores it in `horror.state` and never decides when it advances; the Graph's physical failures and every persisted counter never read it. The persisted `"horror.tell"` counter is restored exactly, so no draw is reused at one epoch and the counter never moves backwards, and a REACH already in flight keeps its stored length (`reach_end_T`, E-HE-36). **Determinism (G4) is defined given the pair (save bytes, `restore_epoch`)**: the same pair replays identically (strike lengths, positions, marks, `state_hash`), tests pin the epoch, and a restore that advances the epoch changes only the lengths of REACHes not yet begun. Nothing physical is re-keyed: mark seeds, LURK waypoint choice and L3 timing are pure integer hashes of ids, the run index and `HE_HASH_SEED` through `he_hash` (below), so the trail and the positions the player can read in the world replay exactly (Pillar 1); they are not threat draws, since the REACH length is Horror's only draw. No wall clock and no global RNG (H9). **`he_hash`** *(defined 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier text said "pure integer hash" with no function or sign rule)*: `he_hash(k1, k2, k3, salt) = lsr(mix64( mix64(k1 ⊕ HE_HASH_SEED) ⊕ mix64(k2 ⊕ salt) ⊕ (k3 × GOLDEN) ), 1)`, on the kernel's pinned `mix64`, `lsr` and `GOLDEN` (kernel D.10) with the intended wrap on the multiplication; the final logical shift makes the result non-negative (63 bits), so every `mod` in this GDD acts on a non-negative integer and no reduction depends on a sign convention. `HE_HASH_SEED` defaults to `0x4845` (any fixed integer; changing it re-rolls every mark seed, LURK waypoint and L3 timing). The salts are fixed constants: `SALT_MARK` 1, `SALT_WP` 2, `SALT_L3_START` 3, `SALT_L3_STRENGTH` 4, `SALT_L3_DUR` 5. Callers: mark seed `he_hash(mark_id, 0, 0, SALT_MARK)`; waypoint rank `he_hash(entity_id, dwell_index, anchor_local_key, SALT_WP)`; L3 `h1`, `h2`, `h3` = `he_hash(emitter_id, run_n, 0, SALT_L3_START)`, `…SALT_L3_STRENGTH)`, `…SALT_L3_DUR)`. Golden vectors are pinned by AC-HE-139. -> ADR candidate (4): a shared pure-integer presentation hash with Lighting LO-19. *Cites.* KRN D.10, D.12, H9.

286	The record's `state` takes one of six values: `LURK`, `STALK`, `REACH`, `STRIKE`, `RETREAT`, `TRANSIT`. The first five are the cycle; `TRANSIT` is a **sixth value, additive** to the five the audio facts need (C-HE-17): relocation through a hull needs a visible place in the machine and has no position. "Permitted act" is what the state may do to the world. Dormancy (HE-21) is not a state: a record whose body is unloaded is frozen in whatever state it holds, with no step.

314	1. **Restore-first.** A run that follows a restore re-checks the predicate for any record in REACH (HE-41) before any other guard.

If `tell_epoch != last_seen_tell_epoch`: zero the five epoch counters and empty `gouged_seg_ids`, set `last_seen_tell_epoch := tell_epoch`, and take a record in REACH to a fizzle (HE-17: no harm, no cooldown consumed) and a record in STRIKE out of its hold, each going to RETREAT in this run (a new `tell_epoch` means the previous breach is over) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; then LURK → STALK (the locus body is the record's body; a record found in RETREAT or STALK passes through LURK first, never skipping it, E-HE-16) or LURK / STALK / RETREAT → TRANSIT (another body; a departure from an unloaded body is allowed, HE-20, and is the only act an unloaded record performs); a record already in TRANSIT retargets to the new locus body (HE-20). 316	3. **Dormancy** *(after the registration reconciliation of HE-34, which runs between guards 2 and 3)*. The record's body is not loaded and the record is not in TRANSIT → no step (HE-21). (A TRANSIT record has no body; its wait for an unloaded destination is HE-21's second rule.)

337	#### Cycle timing at the placeholders
338	
339	Minimum interval between two strike resolutions for a seat that has not moved is `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS + UNFOLD_LO` = 395 ticks (6.6 s) when the horror is already in reach range. `UNFOLD_TICKS` is `5 × rng_int(19, 36)`: 18 equally likely values from 95 to 180 with mean 137.5, so the mean interval is 437.5 ticks (7.3 s) and the longest is 480 ticks (8.0 s). That is a lower bound: after a strike the horror retreats (96 ticks out at `V_CREEP_MPX`, inside the cooldown), turns at `cooldown_until_T` and walks back at `V_HUNT_MPX` (64 ticks, 65 on the run grid), so the realised period of a seat that does not move is `UNFOLD_TICKS + STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS + 65` = 460 to 545 ticks (7.7 to 9.1 s), mean 502.5 (registered formula HE-F15). The time to a third strike for a seat that never moves, and the share of minimum-length breaches that contain a third REACH start (none), are derived in HE-F16 and are not carried here.

384	## Formulas
385	
386	Conventions. Every simulated quantity is an **integer** (ticks, base px, milli-px, basis points, permille, deci-joules, milli-degrees), because anything Horror hashes or replicates must be bit-identical on replay (kernel D.12 `state_hash`, H9): no float, no `sqrt`, no wall clock. Distances are compared as squared integers. Two formulas are analysis only and use real arithmetic (HE-F16's Poisson term and HE-F18's presentation alpha); neither is ever hashed or replicated. `ceil5(x)` rounds `x` up to the next multiple of `HORROR_RUN_TICKS` (5, DERIVED from the hook divisor, HE-4). Locked constants are cited by registry name with the registry value; the Graph's constants (`C_TILE`, `FOOTPRINT_MAX_Q`, `FOOTPRINT_MAX_GOUGE_BP`, `RUPTURE_HP`, `BREACH_HP`, `STRESS_HOLD_STEPS`, registered 2026-10-27) are cited with the registry value and their Life-Support Graph line and never restated as Horror's own. Each two-bound relation below is a **registry-formula candidate** (reflexion 2: register the formula, not only its constants); the registry entries are written from this final text by a later stage, never from the specialist drafts. `ceil_div(a, b) = (a + b − 1) div b` for `a >= 0`, `b > 0`; `he_hash` is defined in HE-42; every integer division in this section is on a non-negative operand *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. `[PH]` is a placeholder; ★ marks a value a neighbour quotes.
387	
388	### HE-F1 Per-window footprint budget
389	
390	The per-window footprint budget formula is defined as:
391	
392	`n_w ≤ HE_FOOTPRINT_BUDGET = MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP − STRESS_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN;  n_run ≤ MAX_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN;  2 × MAX_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN ≤ HE_FOOTPRINT_BUDGET`
393	
394	**Variables:**
395	
396	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
397	|---|---|---|---|---|
398	| `n_w` | int | 0..8 | block (`fp_count` for `fp_window`) | Horror's accepted M17 calls in one Graph window, where a window is *the deposits the next `graph.propagate` run drains*: writes at `T` in `[6k, 6k+5]` drain at the Graph run at `6(k+1)` (HE-29) |
399	| `n_run` | int | 0..4 | block | Accepted M17 calls in one `horror.step` run |
400	| `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP` | int | 16 (CITED) | Life-Support Graph, registry (LSG:807) | The Graph's honoured M17 writes per run |
401	| `STRESS_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN` | int | 1..16, [PH] 8 (CITED) | Attention, registry | Attention's claim on the same cap; Horror leaves it whole |
402	| `MAX_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN` ★ | int | 1..4, [PH] 4 | Horror | Per-run cap so that the two Horror runs that can share one window sum to the budget |
403	| `HE_FOOTPRINT_BUDGET` | int | DERIVED 8 | this formula | Never registered with a free value |
404	
405	**Output Range:** `n_w` in 0..8 and `n_run` in 0..4. Over-budget writes are *not attempted* and are counted `horror_footprints_withheld`; in nominal play that counter is 0 (a defect signal, never a gameplay state). 411	### HE-F2 Strike geometry and walk-out time
412	
413	The strike geometry and walk-out formula is defined as:
414	
415	`hit(seat) = living(seat) ∧ ¬DOWNED(seat) ∧ ¬DEAD(seat) ∧ actor_section(seat) = section(P) ∧ room_at(seat) = room_at(P) ∧ (dx² + dy²) < R_SNAP_PX² ∧ exogenous_permitted(actor_section(seat));   t_out(V, o)` is the first tick count `n` at which a straight walk in octant `o` stands outside the disc, which for a cardinal octant is `ceil(R_SNAP_PX / V)` and for a diagonal octant is the first `n` with `2 × floor(181 × V × n / 256)² >= R_SNAP_PX²` (Body's axis step, BDY-13, with `sub` reset to 0 when the walk starts, BDY-12); `t_out_max(V)` is the maximum over the 8 octants *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier `t_out(V) = ceil(R_SNAP_PX / V)` was the cardinal case only; a diagonal walk-out takes one tick longer)*
416	
417	with `dx = seat.x − P.x` and `dy = seat.y − P.y`, the seat's foot point read after `body.integrate` on the resolving tick (HE-3).

The strict disc is why 36 ticks suffice on a cardinal octant (37 on a diagonal one, see the Output Range). A seat 60 px west of `P` but in the next room (different `room_at`) is not hit. Two seats at `dx = 10` and `dx = 50` in the same room are each hit once: two `apply_suit_damage` calls, one per seat. A DOWNED seat inside the disc is skipped.

436	### HE-F3 Integrity after k strikes (the `STRIKE_BP` two-bound)
437	
438	The integrity-after-k-strikes formula is defined as:
439	
440	`I_k = max(0, I_0 − k × STRIKE_BP);   k_fail(I) = floor((I − SUIT_HP_FAIL) / STRIKE_BP) + 1;   bounds: SUIT_HP_FULL − SUIT_HP_OK < STRIKE_BP  and  2 × STRIKE_BP < SUIT_HP_FULL − SUIT_HP_FAIL  and  SUIT_PATCH_CAP_BP − STRIKE_BP ≥ SUIT_HP_FAIL` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
441	
442	**Variables:**
443	
444	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
445	|---|---|---|---|---|
446	| `I_0`, `I` | int bp | 0..`SUIT_HP_FULL` | Suit (Horror never reads it) | Suit integrity before the first strike |
447	| `STRIKE_BP` ★ | int bp | 3001..3500, [PH] 3200 | Horror (Suit-scale amount) | One strike's integrity cost; the interval is derived from the three bounds (the third is new, *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*) |
448	| `SUIT_HP_FULL` / `SUIT_HP_OK` / `SUIT_LEAK_HP` / `SUIT_HP_FAIL` | int bp | 10000 / 7000 / 5000 / 2500 (CITED) | Suit, registry | Rung thresholds |
449	| `SUIT_PATCH_CAP_BP` | int bp | 6000 default, range 5100..6900 (CITED) | Suit, registry | Cap of `patch_integrity`; no passive regeneration exists. The third bound needs `cap >= STRIKE_BP + SUIT_HP_FAIL`: 5700 at the default `STRIKE_BP`, 6000 over the whole `STRIKE_BP` range. The registered floor of 5100 does not satisfy it, so the data load rejects that pairing rather than letting one strike kill a patched suit; a cross-GDD note to Suit asks for the range floor to follow (Open Question 34) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |

The third bound means **a single strike never kills a patched suit**: the patch cap is a ceiling and `cap − STRIKE_BP >= SUIT_HP_FAIL` (2800 left at the default, exactly 2500 at the corner `STRIKE_BP` 3500 with cap 6000, which is not below `SUIT_HP_FAIL`); without it the registered ranges allowed a one-strike death (cap 5100..5699 at `STRIKE_BP` 3200, or `STRIKE_BP` 3501..3749 at cap 6000), which would break the told-strikes promise of Pillar 2 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. **`STRIKE_BP` is not a lethality dial inside its registered range**; the dials are attempts per breach, inattention (HE-F16's `p`), breaches per session and repair availability. 457	### HE-F4 CHILL cumulative bound
458	
459	The CHILL cumulative bound formula is defined as:
460	
461	`ΔT_mC(Q) = floor(1000 × Q / (C_TILE × n_tiles));   CHILL_EPOCH_MAX_DJ = CHILL_DEPOSITS_PER_EPOCH_MAX × CHILL_STEP_DJ;   lint: ΔT_mC(CHILL_EPOCH_MAX_DJ) at n_tiles_min ≤ CHILL_EPOCH_MAX_MC;   runtime: deposit iff T_c − ΔT_mC(CHILL_STEP_DJ) ≥ COLD_DMG_ONSET_MC + CHILL_MARGIN_MC;   CHILL_STEP_DJ ≤ FOOTPRINT_MAX_Q`
462	
463	**Variables:**
464	
465	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
466	|---|---|---|---|---|
467	| `Q` | int dJ | 0..`CHILL_EPOCH_MAX_DJ` | this formula | Heat removed by one deposit or one epoch of deposits |
468	| `C_TILE` | int dJ per °C per tile | 3000 | Life-Support Graph, registry (LSG:458, :937; CITED) | Heat capacity per tile |
469	| `n_tiles` | int | compartment tile count | Layout | Tiles in the deposited compartment |
470	| `n_tiles_min` | int | smallest authored compartment | Layout, Derelict Authoring *(provisional — not published; 8 assumed in the example)* | Worst case for the lint |
471	| `T_c` | int mC | −40000..70000+ | Graph `compartment(cid)` | The compartment's current temperature |
472	| `COLD_DMG_ONSET_MC` | int mC | −15000, range −25000..−5000 (CITED) | Life-Support Graph, registry | Where cold begins to harm a body |
473	| `CHILL_MARGIN_MC` | int mC | 2000..10000, [PH] 5000 | Horror | Runtime margin kept above the onset |
474	| `CHILL_STEP_DJ` ★ | int dJ | 1000..`FOOTPRINT_MAX_Q`, [PH] 3000 | Horror | One deposit; `FOOTPRINT_MAX_Q` 20000 is the Graph's cap (registry, LSG:912, CITED) |
475	| `CHILL_DEPOSITS_PER_EPOCH_MAX` | int | 1..48, [PH] 24 | Horror | Deposits per `tell_epoch` |
476	| `CHILL_EPOCH_MAX_MC` | int mC | 2000..8000, [PH] 5000 | Horror | Lint ceiling on the epoch total |
477	
478	**Output Range:** one deposit in a 20-tile room is 50 mC; one epoch's maximum is 1200 mC (20 tiles), 2000 mC (12 tiles), 3000 mC (8 tiles). A deposit whose runtime check fails, or whose epoch cap is spent, is **not made** (counters `horror_chill_withheld_cold`, `horror_chill_withheld_cap`); the rime mark is **still laid** in those two cases (ring-only: the mark is a true surface record that the web passed, not a thermal claim), and withheld in the third case only, a coolant fitting within `FITTING_CLEARANCE_PX` (HE-31), where neither deposit nor mark is made.
479	
480	**Example:** `CHILL_EPOCH_MAX_DJ = 24 × 3000 = 72000`. In a 20-tile room `ΔT = 1000 × 72000 / (3000 × 20) = 1200` mC (1.2 °C); the lint at `n_tiles_min` 8 gives 3000 mC ≤ 5000, pass. Runtime: the threshold is `−15000 + 5000 = −10000` mC. A room at −9000 mC deposits (`−9000 − 50 = −9050 ≥ −10000`); a room at −9990 mC withholds (`−10040 < −10000`). *Why this is bookkeeping:* taking a 20 °C, 20-tile room below the Graph's COOL band (under 10 °C) needs `10000 mC × 3000 × 20 / 1000 = 600000` dJ, which is 200 deposits at 3000, and Horror is capped at 24 per epoch; the rime on the floor is a surface mark, and no instrument or body cue disagrees with it (HE-27).
481	
482	**Registry candidate:** `chill_cumulative_bound`.

484	### HE-F5 REACH reaction bound
485	
486	The REACH reaction bound formula is defined as:
487	
488	`UNFOLD_LO ≥ ceil5( t_out_max(V_WALK) + REACT_ALLOW_TICKS_HORROR + INPUT_LATENCY_TICKS + 1 );   UNFOLD_LO mod HORROR_RUN_TICKS = 0;   UNFOLD_HI ≥ UNFOLD_LO;   UNFOLD_TICKS = HORROR_RUN_TICKS × ceil_div( rng_int(UNFOLD_LO / 5, UNFOLD_HI / 5) × UNFOLD_SCALE_PCT, 100 )`  *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the bound now uses `t_out_max`, the slowest of Body's 8 octants (37 ticks, diagonal), carries an explicit input-latency term, and the drawn length can be lengthened, never shortened, by the accessibility scale)*
489	
490	The `+ 1` is the kernel's command application at `apply_tick ≥ T + 1` (KRN D.4): a walk command issued on the last reaction tick moves the seat one tick later. **Tick-indexing convention** (stated once; the slack below is derived under it) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the REACH begins on the Horror run at tick `R` (`reach_start_T`), which executes after `body.integrate` of tick `R` (HE-3); a command the player issues during tick `R + a` is applied at `apply_tick >= R + a + 1` and first moves the seat in the `body.integrate` of tick `R + a + 1`; the strike resolves on the Horror run at `R + U` after that tick's `body.integrate`, so the seat has taken `U − a` steps and is clear iff `U − a >= t_out_max`, that is `U >= a + t_out_max` (91 for `a` = 54 on a diagonal octant). The bound above carries the `+ 1` on top of that count as a deliberate margin, so under this convention the exact slack at `U` = 95 is 4 ticks (5 cardinal), and the 3 (4) quoted in this document is the conservative figure that also spends the margin; AC-HE-130 pins the real kernel order, and a kernel change that applied commands later than `T + 1` would consume the margin first. `rng_int` is drawn from `rng_derive(world_seed, "horror.tell", threat_counter(counter))`, where `threat_counter(c) = c + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE × restore_epoch` is the kernel's one restore-epoch derivation (kernel D.10; HE-42; user ruling X8/D16) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)*; the stream is Horror's REACH length only and is **not** a tell length (HE-9). The scale is applied after the draw in integer order, `UNFOLD_TICKS = 5 × ceil_div(draw × UNFOLD_SCALE_PCT, 100)` (draw 21 at scale 105: `ceil_div(2205, 100) = 23`, so 115); the rounding order is fixed, so there is no sign or rounding ambiguity *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
491	
492	**Variables:**
493	
494	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
495	|---|---|---|---|---|
496	| `R_SNAP_PX` | int px | 72 | HE-F2 | Disc radius |
497	| `t_out_max(V_WALK)` | int ticks | 37 | HE-F2 (Body's stepper, 8 octants) | The slowest walk-out: a diagonal octant |
498	| `INPUT_LATENCY_TICKS` | int ticks | 0..3 fit the current `UNFOLD_LO`; [PH] 0, **unmeasured** | Horror (a spike row, AC-HE-131) | Input-to-motion and display latency (controller poll, render, display). The 3 ticks of slack at `UNFOLD_LO` 95 are its allowance (50 ms); a measured value of 4 or more raises the bound to 100 and `UNFOLD_LO` must move with it (re-derive HE-F13, HE-F15, HE-F16, AC-HE-12, AC-HE-88, AC-HE-91, AC-HE-92, Game Feel; Open Question 17) *(new 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
499	| `UNFOLD_SCALE_PCT` | int percent | 100..200, default 100 | Horror (accessibility setting, persisted in `horror.state`) | Lengthens each drawn `UNFOLD_TICKS` after the draw (`ceil_div`, then × 5), never shortens, so the bound above still holds at every value; it is a world option that takes effect at the next REACH begin and shows nothing in the world (AT-24: no caption, no indicator); replays and saves carry it (HE-41); it changes only through the host command `horror_set_unfold_scale(pct)` *(name provisional)*, a command with `HOST` origin that is hashed in the replay log like any command, applied at its `apply_tick`, range-checked 100..200 and refused otherwise (a lint refuses any other writer), so the field is never written outside the command stream *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; the F13 and F16 figures are stated at scale 100 *(new 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
500	| `V_WALK` | int px/tick | 2 (CITED) | Player Controller, registry | Escaping speed |
501	| `REACT_ALLOW_TICKS_HORROR` | int ticks | 30..90, [PH] 54 | Horror (**unsourced**, C-HE-27; never Attention's `REACT_ALLOW_TICKS` 180) | Reaction allowance: the ticks from the limb entering the cone to the walk command; validated by the blind-legibility playtest |
502	| `UNFOLD_LO`, `UNFOLD_HI` ★ | int ticks | `UNFOLD_LO` 95, `UNFOLD_HI` 180, [PH]; both multiples of 5 | Horror | Telegraph length range |
503	| `counter` | int | ≥ 0 | block (`"horror.tell"` counter) | Incremented in the same block write as the draw; persisted and restored exactly; a restore never rerolls a REACH in flight (only the stream key, through `restore_epoch` inside `threat_counter`, differs after a restore, HE-42) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)* |
504	
505	**Output Range:** `UNFOLD_TICKS` takes 18 equally likely values, 95, 100, …, 180, mean 137.5 ticks (2.29 s). Bound at the placeholders: `t_out_max(V_WALK) 37 + 54 + 0 + 1 = 92`, rounded up to 95; **3 ticks of unclaimed slack** (4 on the cardinal octants, where `36 + 54 + 1 = 91`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier 4 ticks used the cardinal 36; Body's octant stepper makes a diagonal walk-out 37)*. The 3 ticks (50 ms) are the whole allowance for `INPUT_LATENCY_TICKS`; the term is unmeasured, so Open Question 17 and AC-HE-131 carry the measurement. The carrier line is informative: `t_out_max(V_CARRY) 73 + 54 + 1 = 128` (127 on a cardinal octant) against 95 leaves 40 ticks available for 72 (73 diagonal) needed; rounded to the draw grid it is 130, so a carrier who does not drop the cargo is clear on the 11 draws 130..180 and **is struck on the other 7 of 18 draws (38.9 %)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the figure is now explicit)*.
506	
507	**Example:** counter 7 draws `rng_int(19, 36) = 22`, so `UNFOLD_TICKS = 110` and `reach_end_T = reach_start_T + 110`. A walker who reacts in 54 ticks is clear with at least 3 ticks to spare (4 on a cardinal octant) at every legal draw. A carrier who does not drop the cargo can walk out only when `UNFOLD_TICKS ≥ 130` (`128` rounded up to the next draw value), which is 11 of the 18 draws (61.1 %), so it is struck on 7 of 18 (38.9 %); a carrier who drops the cargo inside the reaction budget becomes a walker. C-HE-8 states the carrier case as intended, and the user ruled it so on 2026-10-27.

536	### HE-F7 Mark ring eviction, lifetime and ageing
537	
538	The mark ring eviction, lifetime and ageing formula is defined as:
539	
540	`insert of kind K at its quota evicts argmin(mark_id) over kind = K;   insert of a SMEAR into a full ring evicts argmin(mark_id) over kind = SMEAR;   n_other_max = MARK_QUOTA_RIME + MARK_QUOTA_HAIRLINES + MARK_QUOTA_STRUCK;   life_left ← life_left − HORROR_RUN_TICKS per run while the mark's section is loaded, removed at life_left ≤ 0;   stage = min(2, floor(3 × (MARK_LIFE_TICKS − life_left) / MARK_LIFE_TICKS));   smear_retention_ticks = (MAX_MARKS − n_other_max) × MARK_SPACING_PX × 1000 / V_CREEP_MPX;   MARK_LIFE_TICKS ≥ smear_retention_ticks ≥ TRAIL_TARGET_TICKS;   MAX_MARKS − n_other_max ≥ ceil(TRAIL_TARGET_TICKS × V_CREEP_MPX / (MARK_SPACING_PX × 1000))` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
541	
542	**Variables:**
543	
544	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
545	|---|---|---|---|---|
546	| `mark_id` | int | ≥ 1, never reused | block counter | Insertion order |
547	| `kind` | enum | SMEAR, RIME, HAIRLINES, STRUCK | block | Mark kind (HE-27) |
548	| `MAX_MARKS` | int | `n_other_max + 19`..48 (32..48 at the placeholders), [PH] 32 | Horror | Ring size. Raised from 24 to 32 in the design review (at 24 the smear history was `(24 − 9) × 96 = 1440` ticks, below the 1800 target); the range's floor now follows the quotas, so the range no longer contradicts its own relation *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; a registry request |
549	| `MARK_LIFE_TICKS` | int ticks | `smear_retention_ticks`..54000 (1824 is the derived floor at the placeholders; 3600 is the lowest authored value), [PH] 18000 | Horror | Lifetime of a mark in a loaded section; the lower bound is asserted at load *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
550	| `MARK_SPACING_PX` | int px | 48..144, [PH] 96 | Horror | One SMEAR per this much travel (two tiles); plus one touch-down SMEAR per REACH start |
551	| `CHILL_SPACING_PX` | int px | 192..768, [PH] 384 | Horror | One CHILL deposit and rime mark per this much travel, and at each LURK dwell start |
552	| `n_other_max` | int | DERIVED 13 | the three quotas | `MARK_QUOTA_RIME` 7 + `MARK_QUOTA_HAIRLINES` 3 + `MARK_QUOTA_STRUCK` 3. The rime quota is `ceil(MAX_MARKS / (CHILL_SPACING_PX / MARK_SPACING_PX + 1))` = `ceil(32 / 5)` = 7 (one rime per five ring slots of creep); the other two follow the three-strike ladder. Asserted at data load as arithmetic (`n_other_max + 19 <= MAX_MARKS`), never as a runtime-derived fixture *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
553	| `MARK_QUOTA_RIME` / `MARK_QUOTA_HAIRLINES` / `MARK_QUOTA_STRUCK` | int | 1..12 / 1..6 / 1..6, [PH] 7 / 3 / 3, and `sum + 19 <= MAX_MARKS` | Horror | Per-kind ring quotas (HE-30); an insert at quota evicts the oldest of its own kind *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
554	| `TRAIL_TARGET_TICKS` | int ticks | 1800..3600, [PH] 1800 | game-designer target (the hidden-entity investigation window), not a runtime value | The trail an investigator arriving up to 30 s late should still find |
555	| `V_CREEP_MPX` | int | 1000 | HE-F6 | Creep speed |
556	| `MARKS_PER_RUN_MAX` | int | 1..4, [PH] 2 | Horror | Inserts per run; over the cap, priority STRUCK, then HAIRLINES, then RIME, then SMEAR; a dropped insert is counted `horror_marks_withheld` |
557	
558	**Output Range:** `stage` in {0, 1, 2}: exactly three frame stages for smear and rime (and two for hairlines), so physical age is readable without a meter (Pillar 1) and no continuous value is drawn. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* `smear_retention_ticks` is now a **guaranteed minimum**, because the quotas fix `n_other_max` at 13: at the placeholders `(32 − 13) × 96 × 1000 / 1000 = 1824` ticks at creep speed, at or above `TRAIL_TARGET_TICKS` 1800 whatever the history (an 18000-tick CALM LURK fills the rime quota and no more; a 3600-tick breach fills the HAIRLINES and STRUCK quotas and no more, the oldest of a kind being replaced); more smear history, up to 2112 ticks with only ten others resident, is available but not guaranteed. At `V_HUNT_MPX` the same ring holds `19 × 96 × 1000 / 1500 = 1216` ticks, below the target: the BREACH approach trail is short-lived by construction (the horror covers distance faster than a smear can age), the hidden-entity investigation window is defined on the creep trail, and the shortfall is accepted and logged (Open Question 20). The touch-down SMEAR of each REACH is a SMEAR and competes with the travel smears, but REACHes occur only in BREACH, where that shortfall is already accepted. The ring, not the lifetime, is the binding bound on a creeping horror; the lifetime exists so a frozen loaded body does not keep stale marks forever.
559	
560	**Example:** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* the ring is full at 32 with 3 hairline marks, 3 STRUCK marks, 7 rime marks and 19 smears. A new smear evicts the oldest smear and never a hairline; a fourth HAIRLINES mark evicts the oldest HAIRLINES mark and nothing else; an eighth rime evicts the oldest rime. There is always a smear to evict because `32 > 13`. The relation `MAX_MARKS − n_other_max >= ceil(TRAIL_TARGET_TICKS × V_CREEP_MPX / (MARK_SPACING_PX × 1000))` = 19 is an arithmetic assertion the data load makes: `13 + 19 = 32` passes, and a quota set summing to 14 with `MAX_MARKS` 32 fails the load. Ageing: a mark with `life_left` 12000 has age 6000 and `stage = floor(3 × 6000 / 18000) = 1`; at `life_left` 5999 the age is 12001 and the stage is 2.

564	### HE-F8 Target selection from `lux_pm`
565	
566	The target selection formula is defined as:
567	
568	`candidates = { s : living(s) ∧ ¬DOWNED(s) ∧ ¬IN_POD(s) ∧ actor_section(s) ∈ body_scope ∧ lit(s) };   target = argmax over candidates of (lux_pm(s), −seat_id);   candidates = ∅ ⇒ target = ANCHOR (HE-16 (3))`
569	
570	`body_scope` is `locus_body` in TELL, BREACH and SUBSIDING and the record's own body in CALM. Nothing is stored between runs.
571	
572	**Variables:**
573	
574	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
575	|---|---|---|---|---|
576	| `lux_pm(s)` | int permille | 0..1000 | Emitter `lux(ref)` | The seat's illumination; the owner stands in their own light (EM-21), so a seat with its lamp on reads 1000 |
577	| `lit(s)` | bool | — | derived here: `lux_pm(s) >= LIT_ON_PM` (150, CITED) | Stateless, recomputed every run, nothing stored. **Not the Emitter's `lit` bit** (a hysteresis on `act_lux_pm`, which excludes the owner's own beam and the BEACON; a lone lamp-on player reads `act_lux_pm` 0) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
578	| `seat_id` | int | ≥ 0 | Body | Tie-break: lowest wins |
579	| `ANCHOR` | position | Layout `anchor_geometry` | HE-16 (3) | The target when no candidate is lit |
580	
581	**Output Range:** a seat id or ANCHOR; one `lux(ref)` read per candidate per run, zero probes (HE-43).
582	
583	**Example:** seat A `lux_pm` 1000 (lamp on), seat B 0 (dark): target A. Seat A switches the lamp off: no lit candidate, target ANCHOR on the next run, and nothing remembers A (the target is not persisted). A thrown Chemlight pool reads 700 only for a seat that stands in it; the horror targets whichever *seat* is lit, never the pool (a pool is not a seat, HE-13). Two lit seats at 1000 and 1000: the lower `seat_id` wins; a stateless argmax can alternate as lamps change (C-HE-19, Vertical Slice). *Further cases (design review):* a seat with its lamp off under a lit fixture reading 400 is lit (`400 >= 150`) and is the target while a dark seat is not; a seat with its lamp off whose only light is the BEACON's sweep is lit only on the runs where `lux_pm >= 150` (it counts in `lux_pm`, not in `act_lux_pm`) and the next run's target may differ, but a REACH already begun keeps its locked P; a seat with its lamp on standing in a 400 fixture pool and a seat with its lamp off in a 700 Chemlight pool: the lamp-on seat reads 1000 and wins, so the argmax is the lamp, not the amount *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.

585	**Registry candidate:** `horror_target_rule`.

587	### HE-F9 Ingress timing and entry choice
588	
589	The ingress timing and entry choice formula is defined as:
590	
591	`transit_until_T = tell_enter_T + INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS;   fallback_T = transit_until_T + STALK_VISIBLE_FLOOR_TICKS;   arrive_T = min{ T ≥ transit_until_T : T mod 5 = 0 ∧ ( legal_entry(T) ∨ (T ≥ fallback_T + INGRESS_MARK_LEAD_TICKS ∧ fallback_entry(T)) ) };   stalk_visible_min = TELL_MIN_TICKS − INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS;   D_entry_max = LURK_STANDOFF_PX + floor(stalk_visible_min × V_CREEP_MPX / 1000);   INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS + STALK_VISIBLE_FLOOR_TICKS + INGRESS_MARK_LEAD_TICKS ≤ TELL_MIN_TICKS` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
592	
593	`legal_entry(T)` selects, among the hull entries of `locus_body` at room-hop distance 1 from the room of the highest-`lux_pm` living seat (none lit or present: the locus section's outermost compartment), a hull segment whose room holds no living seat and which lies at least `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` from every living seat **that is `linked` to it (HE-19)**; ties lowest hop, then lowest room id, then lowest hull-segment id. A *hull entry* is an `anchor_geometry` point of a hull-bearing compartment that lies within `HULL_CONTACT_PX` of a hull face, paired with the lowest id returned by `hull_segments_near(section_id, anchor_px, HULL_CONTACT_PX)`; there is no `solid_in` sampling and no unpublished room-to-segment read. The entry is chosen at the run at `transit_until_T − INGRESS_MARK_LEAD_TICKS` and the ingress mark is laid then (re-chosen under E-HE-34 if it becomes illegal); the body arrives at `transit_until_T`, or at the first later run whose re-chosen entry has had its full mark lead. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Fallback.** `fallback_entry(T)` is the *nearest legal hull anchor*: if no legal entry exists at `fallback_T` (540 ticks after TELL entry at the placeholders, inside `TELL_MIN_TICKS`), the hop-1 and standoff conditions drop out and the entry is the hull entry nearest by room hops to the lit seat's room whose room holds no living seat (ties as above); its mark is laid at `fallback_T` and the body arrives `INGRESS_MARK_LEAD_TICKS` later, no later than `TELL_MIN_TICKS`. Only when every hull room holds a living seat does the record stay in TRANSIT (`horror_ingress_pending`, E-HE-33). **Precondition of `stalk_visible_min`:** the visible-stalk bound below holds only when a legal entry exists at `INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS`; under the fallback the told breach still has a horror and an ingress mark from `fallback_T`, but the visible stalk can be as short as the mark lead before BREACH entry at the shortest tell.
594	
595	**Variables:**
596	
597	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
598	|---|---|---|---|---|
599	| `INGRESS_DELAY_TICKS` ★ | int ticks | 120..360, [PH] 300 | Horror | Earliest ingress after TELL entry |
600	| `TELL_MIN_TICKS` | int ticks | 600 (CITED, DERIVED from `W_MIN_WARNING_S`) | Attention, registry | Shortest tell |
601	| `STALK_VISIBLE_FLOOR_TICKS` | int ticks | 120..360, [PH] 240 | Horror | The least visible stalk the design accepts |
602	| `INGRESS_MARK_LEAD_TICKS` | int ticks | 30..120, [PH] 60 | Horror | The mark precedes the body so a player watching that wall sees the arrival coming |
603	| `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` | int px | 144..288, [PH] 192 | Horror | HE-F14 |
604	| `V_CREEP_MPX` | int milli-px/tick | 1000..1400, [PH] 1000 | Horror | HE-F6 |
605	| `D_entry_max` | int px | derived 492 | this formula | The farthest an entry may lie from the seat for the stalk to close to the standoff before the shortest tell ends |
606	
607	**Output Range:** `stalk_visible_min = 300` ticks (5 s): the entity's presence is published for at least 300 ticks before the shortest tell ends (up to 4 ticks later for run alignment); whether the player *sees* it depends on light. An entry beyond `D_entry_max` still arrives inside the tell but reaches the standoff after BREACH entry (the approach then runs at `V_HUNT_MPX`); it is a tuning and authoring signal, never a rule violation. The relation in the formula's last clause is the dependent bound for the three knobs (their ranges are not independent): 300 + 240 + 60 = 600 at the placeholders *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
608	
609	**Example:** TELL enters at `T = 1200` with a drawn length of 900. `transit_until_T = 1500`; the ingress mark is laid at 1440 and the body registers (E6) at the run at 1500; BREACH begins at 2100, so the stalk is published for 600 ticks. Relation check: `300 + 240 + 60 = 600 ≤ 600` (pass, with no slack at the placeholders) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; `D_entry_max = 192 + 300 = 492` px, covering a one-hop entry in the 288 to 480 px room sizes of the slice. If a seat walks into the chosen room during the 60 ticks of mark lead, the entry is re-chosen by the same rule; the first hairline stays (it is a true mark of where the web touched).
610	
611	**Registry candidate:** `horror_ingress_timing`.

634	### HE-F11 L3 disturbance strength and duration bound
635	
636	The L3 disturbance strength and duration formula is defined as:
637	
638	`S_hi = 1000 − MOD_FLOOR_PM;   strength_pm = L3_STRENGTH_LO_PM + (h2 mod (S_hi − L3_STRENGTH_LO_PM + 1));   dur_ticks = L3_DUR_LO + (h3 mod (L3_DUR_HI − L3_DUR_LO + 1));   start iff h1 mod 1000 < L3_START_PM ∧ T ≥ last_end_T + L3_MIN_GAP_TICKS;   L3_STRENGTH_LO_PM ≤ S_hi`
639	
640	`h1`, `h2`, `h3` are `he_hash(emitter_id, run_n, 0, SALT_L3_START)`, `…SALT_L3_STRENGTH)` and `…SALT_L3_DUR)` (HE-42: non-negative, golden vectors in AC-HE-139), never `rng_derive`. The result enters Lighting's registered `modifier_stack` as the L3 factor, whose floor `MOD_FLOOR_PM` already clamps the chain; Horror never restates or applies that clamp. **Sign convention** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `strength_pm` is a dip **depth**, like Lighting's `DIP_DEPTH_PM` (`M1 = 1000 − DIP_DEPTH_PM` during a dip, LO D.15); Lighting's L3 factor is `M3 = 1000 − strength_pm` (1000 = no dip). **Worked LO-18 example:** `strength_pm` 374 gives `M3 = 626`; with a concurrent gutter `M1 = 700`, an idle tell `M2 = 1000` and `MOD_FLOOR_PM` 600, `m_mod = clamp(floor(700 × 1000 × 626 / 10^6), 600, 1000) = clamp(438, 600, 1000) = 600` (the floor binds); with `M1 = 1000` the same dip is `clamp(626, 600, 1000) = 626`. The reduced-motion cap is stated in Tuning Knobs (`L3_STRENGTH_RM_CAP_PM`).
641	
642	**Variables:**
643	
644	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
645	|---|---|---|---|---|

732	The cycle period formula is defined as:

736	After a strike the horror RETREATs to the nearest waypoint at least `LURK_STANDOFF_PX` from every living seat (HE-17); at `cooldown_until_T` it turns to STALK and walks back at `V_HUNT_MPX` until it is within `REACH_RANGE_PX`; the next REACH may begin only then (HE-14 (e) and (d)).

762	`s_1 = t_arrive;   s_{k+1} = s_k + U_k + STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS + t_back;   T_3 = t_arrive + U_1 + U_2 + U_3 + 2 × (STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS + t_back);   T_2 = t_arrive + U_1 + U_2 + (STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS + t_back);   third REACH starts inside a breach of length B iff s_3 < B;   P_3(λ) = 1 − e^{−λ} × (1 + λ + λ²/2) (fresh suit, I_0 ≥ 8900: three landed strikes kill);   P_2(λ) = 1 − e^{−λ} × (1 + λ) (worn or patched suit, I_0 < 8900: two kill);   λ = E_s × n × p` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*

764	The first four terms are integer simulation arithmetic; `P_death` is design analysis (real arithmetic, never hashed): the probability of at least three landed strikes (fresh suit) or two (worn or patched suit) in a session when strikes arrive as a Poisson process (no passive integrity regeneration exists, so hits accumulate until `patch_integrity`, HE-F3). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* The fresh-suit tail alone understated lethality and was only a lower bound; `k_fail(I) = 3` needs `I >= 8900` (`floor((I − 2500) / 3200) + 1`), so every patched suit (cap at most 6900) and every suit after one landed strike (6800) is in the two-strike state.

807	**Registry candidate:** `hull_act_ladder`.

809	### HE-F18 Presentation interpolation alpha (render side only)
810	
811	The presentation interpolation alpha formula is defined as:
812	
813	`alpha5 = ((T_now − T_run) + tick_alpha) / HORROR_RUN_TICKS;   draw_pos = pos_prev + (pos_curr − pos_prev) × alpha5`
814	
815	This is presentation arithmetic (real numbers, never hashed, never in a SIM block); the rig *pose* is stepped once per run and never tweened (PIPE row 14). It is owed to the Pipeline because the kernel's `tick_alpha` spans one tick, not five (C-HE-14).
816	
817	**Variables:**
818	
819	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
820	|---|---|---|---|---|
821	| `T_now`, `T_run` | int tick | — | Kernel | The presented tick and the tick of the most recent Horror run |
822	| `tick_alpha` | real | [0, 1] | Kernel | Fraction within the current tick |
823	| `pos_prev`, `pos_curr` | int px | — | `horror.view` | Positions at the previous and the latest run |
824	
825	**Output Range:** `alpha5` in [0, 1]. **Example:** two ticks after the run with `tick_alpha` 0.5: `alpha5 = (2 + 0.5) / 5 = 0.5`, the draw position is the midpoint. A rig pose change on any tick that is not a multiple of 5 fails the cadence criterion.
826	
827	**Registry candidate:** none (render-side; owed to the Pipeline).

888	- **If a restore lands INTO STRIKE (E-HE-38)**: the strike's `apply_suit_damage` and M17 calls were made on the entry run and are part of Suit's and the Graph's restored state; STRIKE is only the held snap pose and restoring it issues no second hit. `strike_T`, `seats_hit[]` and `strike_hull_seg` are persisted while the record is in STRIKE (HE-41), so the hit cue is not replayed *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.

890	- **If any restored value is out of range (`strikes_epoch` above `STRIKES_EPOCH_MAX` 13, a mark ring longer than `MAX_MARKS`, a position outside its section, `acc_mpx` ≥ 1000) (E-HE-40)**: restore fails hard with the matching `HORROR_RESTORE_*` code (`RANGE`, `MARK_RING`, `SECTION_UNKNOWN`) and the Save/Load layer refuses the file; nothing is clamped (SL-15). A clamp would hide a corrupt save behind a plausible world.
891	- **If the player dies and the game restarts from the newest autosave (E-HE-41)**: `horror.state` restores with the WORLD blocks, including the `"horror.tell"` counter, exactly. The counter continues from its saved value, but the stream is re-keyed by the restore's `restore_epoch` through the kernel's `threat_counter` (HE-42, user ruling X8/D16, delegated ruling R1), so **the replay does not draw the same `UNFOLD_TICKS` sequence**: a death or loss of play is not a way to scout the telegraph lengths of the next breach, and (Save/Load's constraint) quit and death offer no reroll oracle (a Save & Quit then Continue of the newest `QUIT` generation carries the epoch and replays the same draws, so quitting cannot reroll; a death-stub restore advances it; delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R13/R14)*. The marks, positions and every physical fact are bit-identical to uninterrupted play given the pair (save, `restore_epoch`) (G4); the draws themselves stay inside the legal range, so the fairness bound of HE-F5 holds at every re-keyed draw; what the player learned stays in their head (Pillar 5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
892	- **If an autosave fires during CALM while a LURK stands at the standoff (E-HE-42)**: no Horror gate is needed; CALM is non-lethal by construction (HE-10), no lethal horror is ever adjacent to a seat in a CALM save, and SL-5 is unchanged. If the standoff rule is ever relaxed, SL-5 must be revisited.
893	- **If a record's body is unloaded (E-HE-43)**: the record is frozen, its marks do not age, its disturbances do not run and nothing fast-forwards on reload (HE-21, LS-17), **with one exception: a new `tell_epoch` whose locus body is not that body sends the record to TRANSIT at once (HE-20, guard 2), even though its own body is unloaded, with an egress mark laid in the unloaded section (inserted, not ageing)**. A record in TRANSIT whose destination unloads waits. If an unloaded record is somehow woken with a `last_seen_tell_epoch` that is two or more epochs old (a restored older save), the lazy reset zeroes its five epoch counters and empties `gouged_seg_ids` before any act, so its caps are never bound by a stale epoch *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
894	
895	#### Budgets, registration and determinism
896	
897	- **If `register_subject` (E6) returns false on a first registration (not a duplicate) (E-HE-44)**: the subject reads dark (`lux` 0, `lit` false); that is a **budget defect**, a failing criterion and a lint, never a gameplay state. The horror still moves and strikes (its harm does not depend on being a subject); the defect is that nothing can light it.
898	- **If a stub requests more footprints than the window allows (E-HE-45)**: at most `HE_FOOTPRINT_BUDGET` 8 per window are made, at most `MAX_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN` 4 per run; the rest are not attempted (a trace is a moment, not a queue) and counted `horror_footprints_withheld`. In nominal play the counter is 0; a nonzero count in a build is a defect.
899	- **If a mark insert mutates a packed array element without declaring its dirty key (E-HE-46)**: Godot 4.7 packed-array element writes do not call the setter, so the kernel would miss the change and `state_hash` would differ after a restore. Every mutation of the ring, the disturbance list and the record declares explicit dirty keys; a lint and a save-equivalence criterion enforce it.
900	- **If the same `world_seed`, the same (save, `restore_epoch`) pair and the same inputs are replayed (E-HE-47)**: the strike lengths, positions, marks, disturbance timings and `state_hash` are identical (HE-42). Randomness is `rng_derive` for the REACH length only; mark seeds, LURK waypoints and L3 timing are pure integer hashes of ids, the run index and `HE_HASH_SEED`.
901	
902	#### Hallucination and the Perception Filter
903	
904	- **If the Filter hides a real horror's body from one seat (Vertical Slice class (a), "hidden real entity") (E-HE-48)**: the marks, L3 state, M17 writes, `apply_suit_damage` calls and `horror.view` are bit-identical with and without the hide (HE-32). The limb tip and body are undrawn for that seat, but the touch-down smear at P is a true mark the Filter may not edit, so "a smear appeared under my feet" falsifies the hide at a cost of looking at the floor. The hide collapses when `horror.view` reports a state outside {LURK, RETREAT} *(provisional — Sanity & Hallucination Rules designed in this run)*.
905	- **If a phantom horror co-occurs with a real one (E-HE-49)**: the phantom has no record, no mark, no footprint, no registration and no strike (HE-32); the real one proceeds on its own clock. A seat that flees the phantom can walk into the real disc; "is the floor marked?" is the check, and TellAudit records nothing for the phantom (AT E-53).
906	- **If the Filter shows a crewmate as a horror and a seat harms that crewmate (Vertical Slice class (c)) (E-HE-50)**: that is the friendly-harm act under Interaction and Sanity's gate, not Horror's; no Horror state changes. The rig presenter is only the substitute body; a real horror emits nothing and carries no beam, so the true beam remains a perfect discriminator (HE-2).
907	- **If a seat's own Sanity state makes it see violet fringes or false gauges (E-HE-51)**: Horror's marks, disturbances and positions are TRUTH channel and are not corruptible; the body can be omitted or wholly substituted only by the Filter, and marks never use flesh or violet (HE-31). Horror reads no `PERCEPTION_OUT` block (CR-12).
908	
909	#### Co-op hooks (Vertical Slice and later)
910	
911	- **If two lit seats are in the locus body (E-HE-52)**: the higher `lux_pm` wins; a tie goes to the lower seat id; a stateless argmax can alternate as lamps change, and a hysteresis would need a stored value (C-HE-19, an Open Question). A strike hits every living seat in the disc once, in ascending player id, each as its own `apply_suit_damage` call.
912	- **If a seat is DOWNED by a teammate (friendly harm) or by another cause during a REACH (E-HE-53)**: it is not "living, non-DOWNED" at resolution and is not hit; the REACH completes harmlessly and the record RETREATs. DOWNED and DEAD seats are never candidates (HE-18).
913	- **If a second record is requested while `HORROR_MAX_MVP` is 1 (E-HE-54)**: the request is refused by the data lint and the boot check; at runtime `S_h ≤ HORROR_SUBJECTS_MAX` 2 is a ceiling reserved for the transient during ingress. Rosters per ring and more types are Vertical Slice.
914	- **If a seat is in a different body from `locus_body` (E-HE-55)**: it is not a candidate in TELL, BREACH or SUBSIDING, is never hit, and is not the subject of the predicate (the predicate's argument is Body's `actor_section`, not the Graph's `section_of`). In CALM the candidates are the seats in the record's own body.

951	## Tuning Knobs
952	
953	Every Horror-owned value lives in the per-type data file keyed by `type_id` (HE-5, R26); no behavioural constant lives in code. Every default is a **`[PLACEHOLDER]`** pending playtest, and every row is a candidate for the registry, written from this final text by a later stage. **★ marks a value that a neighbour quotes or that a registered relation binds** (a cross-system fact: another GDD, the registry or an acceptance criterion outside this document reads it); an unstarred knob is Horror-internal. Durations are authored as integer counts of runs (`HORROR_RUN_TICKS` 5) and published in ticks; a duration that is not a multiple of 5 is a data-load failure (HE-4, E-HE-4). "Interacts with" names the formula or neighbour that binds the row; the formula, not the row, is the source of truth for any two-bound.
954	
955	**The dials that move lethality are not in this table.** `STRIKE_BP` cannot change the hits-to-FAILED count inside its registered interval (HE-F3), so "make it more lethal" is a request to change the per-attempt miss rate `p`, the attempts per breach, the breaches per session (Attention's) or repair availability (Suit's). `rng_derive(world_seed, stream_name, counter) = mix64( world_seed ⊕ mix64(fnv64(stream_name)) ⊕ (counter × GOLDEN) )`; `unit = lsr(rng_derive, 11) / 2^53`; `rng_int(lo, hi) = lo + floor(unit × (hi − lo + 1))`

with `lsr(x, n) = (x >> n) & ((1 << (64 − n)) − 1)` for 1 ≤ n ≤ 63 (logical shift); `mix64(z)` = the SplitMix64 finaliser: `z = (z ⊕ lsr(z, 30)) × C1; z = (z ⊕ lsr(z, 27)) × C2; return z ⊕ lsr(z, 31)`; `fnv64` = FNV-1a over the UTF-8 bytes of the name, `h = FNV_OFFSET; for each byte: h = (h ⊕ byte) × FNV_PRIME`, **computed once per stream at registration and cached, never per draw**. Constants as GDScript `int` literals (hex shown for reference only — a hex literal above `0x7FFF…` is not a valid `int` literal): `GOLDEN` = 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 = `-7046029254386353131`; `C1` = 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9 = `-4658895280553007687`; `C2` = 0x94D049BB133111EB = `-7723592293110705685`; `FNV_OFFSET` = 0xCBF29CE484222325 = `-3750763034362895579`; `FNV_PRIME` = 0x100000001B3 = `1099511628211`. **Integer wrap on multiplication is intended** and relied on; the golden vectors below (several have the top bit set) fail at once on an implementation that does not wrap or that uses an arithmetic shift.

**Variables:**
| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
| world_seed | int (64-bit pattern) | any `int` | data file (kernel.clock block; set at new game, persisted) | Per-world seed; stored as the signed `int` with the same bit pattern as the u64 |
| stream_name | string | registered, e.g. `horror.tell` | data file (owner declares) | Names an independent stream |
| counter | int | 0–2^63−1 | calculated (lives in the owner's block, incremented per draw, persisted with it) | Draw index |
| mix64 | fn | bijective 64-bit → 64-bit, full avalanche | constant (SplitMix64 finaliser; **set-once**, ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling, R-17 — the kernel ADR may change it only before the first save format ships) | Mixing function |
| rng_derive | int (64-bit pattern) | any `int` | calculated | Deterministic raw value (print as `hex64`) |
| unit | float | [0, 1) | calculated | 53-bit uniform |
| rng_int | int | [lo, hi] | calculated | Uniform integer in an inclusive range; **requires `lo ≤ hi` and `hi − lo + 1 ≤ 2^32`** |

**Output Range:** `unit` is in `[0, 1)` exactly (the top 53 bits divided by 2^53 can never reach 1). `rng_int` is inclusive at both ends; its bias is at most `span / 2^53 ≤ 2^-21` (there is no modulo, so no modulo bias, and the span cap is what keeps it negligible). A call with `lo > hi` or a span above 2^32 is a caller defect: it returns `lo`, increments `RNG_RANGE_VIOLATION` and reports a violation (CR-19). Pure: the same `(seed, name, counter)` always gives the same value regardless of call order or which other streams drew — which is what lets G3 replay and G4 save-equivalence hold with no RNG state outside blocks. A stream's counter restores with its block, so a save mid-tell reproduces the same tell.
**Golden vectors** (computed with an independent 64-bit reference implementation; these are the acceptance values): `fnv64("horror.tell")` = `0xE500B5B58A7689E2`; `mix64(1)` = `0x5692161D100B05E5`; `mix64(0x8000000000000000)` = `0x25C26EA579CEA98A`; with `world_seed = 0x5EED000000002026`: `rng_derive(seed, "horror.tell", 17)` = `0xB2AA94991B52A02E` → `unit ≈ 0.6979153513` → `rng_int(600, 1800) = 600 + floor(0.6979153513 × 1201) = 600 + 838 = 1438` ticks ≈ 24.0 s; `rng_derive(seed, "horror.tell", 0)` = `0x4988DBEFD7F20FF5`; `rng_derive(seed, "graph.failure", 0)` = `0x0CEEC43F97221B55`; with `world_seed = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF`: `rng_derive(seed, "horror.tell", 1)` = `0x883EA97FED4A4613`. The `horror.tell` / `rng_int(600, 1800)` usage matches Horror's HE-9 stream use (*Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from horror-entities*).

*Maintenance note:* a 63-bit owner-defined key (for example the Graph's `(step_no, subject_id)`) is a valid `counter` for `rng_derive` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format (SL-23))*.

**Restore-epoch re-keying** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1; implements user ruling X8/D16, which stands unchanged)*. The one place a restore epoch enters a draw is a kernel helper; Attention and Horror call it and define no derivation of their own:

`rng_derive_epoch(world_seed, stream_name, rng_counter) = rng_derive( world_seed, stream_name, counter_eff )`, `counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE × restore_epoch`

**Variables:**
| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|----------|------|-------|--------|-------------|
| rng_counter | int | 0 to `RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE − 1` | calculated (lives in the threat owner's `WORLD` block, persisted) | The owner's own stream position; restores exactly and is never rerolled by a restore |
| restore_epoch | int (u32) | 0 to 2^32 − 1 | Save/Load (persisted in the per-slot side file `slot_epoch.bin`, SL-23); the kernel exposes it read-only in the `kernel.clock` read view | Advances by 1 on a death-stub restore, a `FAULT_RECOVERY` and a Continue of any generation other than the newest non-demoted verified `QUIT` generation (in-process or after a fresh process start), so two death restores of one autosave install e + 1 and e + 2; a Continue of that `QUIT` generation carries it unchanged. Save/Load's ACs (AC-SL-142, AC-SL-145) own the advance, carry and durability halves *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14)* |
| RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE | int | fixed 1,048,576 (2^20) | constant (the kernel owns it; value unchanged from the Attention GDD's figure) | Keeps the epoch term from colliding with any reachable `rng_counter` |
| counter_eff | int | 0 to 2^52 − 1 | calculated | The counter handed to `rng_derive`; below 2^63, so D.10's counter range holds |

**Output Range / guards (G5):** `stream_name` hash stays cached and unchanged (only `counter` moves). Preconditions: `0 ≤ rng_counter < RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE` and `0 ≤ restore_epoch ≤ 2^32 − 1`. A call that breaks either is a caller defect: `RNG_COUNTER_RANGE_VIOLATION` increments, a violation is reported (CR-19), and the value is still computed as written (deterministic, never a trap); a `request_restore` carrying an epoch outside the u32 range fails its pre-check `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE` → `FAULTED` (the same path as `TICK_RATE_MISMATCH`). At `restore_epoch = 0` the helper equals plain `rng_derive`. **Scope**: threat draws only (Attention's `attention.tell`, Horror's REACH-length draw). Graph physical failures and every persisted counter call plain `rng_derive` and never read the epoch, so they replay exactly. **Accurate behaviour (replacing the earlier claim that quitting or dying could not move a draw, which was wrong in both directions while the epoch reset on process start)**: every advancing restore (a death-stub restore, a `FAULT_RECOVERY`, a Continue of any generation other than the newest `QUIT` one) yields a new epoch, so a threat draw made after it is never a repeat of the one the earlier run met; a Save & Quit then Continue carries the epoch, so the draws after it are exactly those an uninterrupted run would make, and quitting buys nothing (user ruling D16, delegated ruling R13). The one listed exposure is R14's failure path: if Save/Load's `slot_epoch.bin` write fails or times out, a kill before its next successful write may replay that epoch once (CR-15) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14)*; determinism (G3/G4) is defined given the pair `(save bytes, restore_epoch)`: the same pair replays identically, and tests pin the 
**Example (golden, `world_seed = 0x5EED000000002026`, stream `"horror.tell"`, `rng_counter = 17`):** epoch 0 → `counter_eff = 17` → `0xB2AA94991B52A02E` (`rng_int(600, 1800) = 1438`, the existing vector); epoch 1 → `counter_eff = 1,048,593` → `0x6EFE2D9E722654C6` (`unit ≈ 0.4335659515` → 1120); epoch 2 → `counter_eff = 2,097,169` → `0xA46E009E591F2390` (`unit ≈ 0.6423035037` → 1371). The three differ, as AC KRN-EPO-01 requires.

**D.11 Snapshot size and capture budget**
- **GIVEN** blocks `A (restore_after: [B])` and `B (restore_after: [A])`, or a `restore_after` naming an unregistered block, **WHEN** boot runs, **THEN** `BOOTING → FAULTED` naming the cycle path or the unknown ID; **GIVEN** a 129th block registered at `MAX_BLOCKS = 128`, **THEN** `BOOTING → FAULTED` naming `MAX_BLOCKS`, while 128 blocks boot.
