content.content:
## Summary

Horror Entities is the simulation of the one real, hostile thing in the ship: a single segment-rig creature (one type, one instance, one lurk / stalk / reach / strike / retreat cycle) that turns Attention's abstract "the web has noticed you" into a body at a true position, gated by Attention's told-breach permission, that unfolds a limb onto a locked point and snaps, leaves honest marks and Graph footprints wherever it has been, and can be outwalked, hidden from or locked out but never fought or farmed. Read it if you touch any system that deals harm, writes a footprint, dips a lamp, places a sound on a body or draws a mark, because this document owns the tell composition (additive to Attention's 10-30 s window), the walk-out arithmetic that makes death fair, the truth-channel footprints a hallucination cannot hide, and the acceptance criteria that discharge the Horror half of Attention's, the Graph's, the Emitter's, Lighting's and Suit's must-repeats.

> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Feature` · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `Command & Simulation Layer (designed)`, `Life-Support Graph (designed)`, `Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query (designed in this run)`, `Attention System (designed in this run)`, `Suit & Equipment (designed in this run)`, `Ship Body & Interior Physics (designed in this run)`, `Ship Section & Layout Data Model (designed; `hull_segments_near` and `door_passage` published, HE-19; amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)`, `Save/Load & Versioned Format (designed in this run)`; downstream: `Adaptive Audio & Tells (designed)`, `Perception Filter (designed)`, `Sanity & Hallucination Rules (designed in this run)`

## Overview

Horror Entities is the simulation of the one kind of thing in the ship that is real, hostile and not a machine: a scene-tree-free, integer-only `SIM` block, `horror.state`, advanced by one divisor-5 step hook, `horror.step`, that holds the horror's true position, its behaviour state and the trail it leaves, and that turns Attention's abstract promise ("the web has noticed you") into a body in a room that the player can read, avoid and, if they do not, die to. In one sentence: **it is the web's physical consequence, a single segment-rig creature that lurks in the dark in CALM, stalks toward the light in a TELL, reaches at a point it has locked in a BREACH and then snaps, and that leaves honest marks wherever it has been.**

**The data layer.** The block holds one entity record at MVP (`HORROR_MAX_MVP` 1, type `horror_t01`, a placeholder renamed never aliased): body, section, integer base-px position with sub-pixel residue, behaviour state (`LURK`, `STALK`, `REACH`, `STRIKE`, `RETREAT`, plus `TRANSIT` while it passes through a hull), the locked strike point and the tick its telegraph ends, per-epoch strike, gouge and rupture counts, and a persisted counter for its one random stream, `"horror.tell"`. Beside the record sits a bounded, persisted **mark ring** (`MAX_MARKS`, wet iridescent smear, branching rime, radial hairlines, and the STRUCK burst that records a hit) and the published state of its **light disturbance** (L3) on nearby fixtures. Everything is derived from three reads and nothing else: Attention's committed `attention.view` (phase, locus, the permission predicate), the Emitter's `lux(ref)` for the seats it might prefer, and Layout's room graph for its movement. It writes the world in exactly three ways and no others: Class B footprint deposits through the Graph's `deposit_trace` (M17: CHILL, GOUGE and RUPTURE; never STRESS, which is Attention's alone), Class B `apply_suit_damage` on a body inside a telegraphed strike disc, and its own published state (marks, disturbances, `horror.view`) that Lighting and the presenters read. It is a registered Emitter subject (it can be lit and therefore seen) and it emits nothing, occludes nothing and casts no shadow. Its position is its own, moved by Body's pure `LocomotionStep` against Layout's solids; it is never a Body fact, a `CharacterBody2D` or a physics query. It holds no hit points, no aggro, threat, alert or awareness value of any kind, and no meter: the only thing it remembers is where it has been (marks) and what it has already done this epoch (counts).

**The player-facing effect.** The player does not meet a monster; they meet weather with intent. In CALM they may glimpse something long and low at the edge of their lamp, never nearer than a few tiles, and later find a wet streak or a forked white rime where it passed: the ship is not empty. A sighting in CALM is information and never a danger: the thing cannot hurt you in CALM (HE-11), but it tells you which body it lives in and that its trail and rime are fresh, and a player who reads that changes the route they take, whether the lamp is on and which job they do first. In a TELL, while Attention's creaking and filaments rise everywhere, a hairline appears on a hull face, a fixture nearby dips on its own irregular rhythm, and the thing comes in through the wall toward whoever is carrying light. When the TELL becomes a BREACH it closes at a pace the player can outwalk, plants its body, and unfolds one long jointed limb across the floor until the tip rests, motionless, on the spot where it has decided to strike. The player has one to three seconds to see the limb and step off that spot. If they do, nothing happens to them and the ship pays in scratched hull; if they do not, the suit takes a hit and the floor keeps a hairline burst where it landed (a miss leaves only the smear); the second hit opens a leak and staggers the body to a walk, and three such hits take the body down. The horror then retreats, and the cycle repeats until the breach subsides. Nothing the player carries can kill it, nothing it does can be farmed, and it leaves nothing behind but its trail.

**The contract this GDD owns.** Horror is the only gameplay system whose lethal acts are neither player-originated nor environmental, so it is where the Graph's exported requirement ("every non-player exogenous source must be preceded by that system's own Pillar 2 tell of 10-30 s", LSG:144) meets a body. Attention satisfies the 10-30 s at the breach level (AT-15); Horror **repeats** the permission predicate `exogenous_permitted(section)` at its three check points (REACH begin, STRIKE entry, every M17 RUPTURE or GOUGE call), adds two layers that are *additive and never a substitute* (the visible stalk and the REACH telegraph at a locked point), and publishes the facts a `TellAudit` replay needs. It discharges the Horror half of LSG:1063 and the crew-body scope of AT-15 R15. It is also the second GDD to land on the Emitter's "the beam reveals, never repels" rail (EM:89) and adopts it verbatim.

**What the game loses without it.** Without Horror, a breach on a clean ship is "nearly a non-event" and *commit* dominates *abort* (AT-11): restraint becomes decoration, Pillar 3 is hollow and the "chaos" half of Pillar 2 is empty. The Graph's exogenous footprint kinds have no caller, so a hidden real entity has no trail and Pillar 4's class (a) has no substance. Death-is-a-bitch (the user's decision) would arrive only through plumbing (decompression, cold), never through something that moves. Adaptive Audio would have no body to place a creak on, and Lighting's L3 disturbance would remain a stub. The core hypothesis (the boarding-and-breach loop is tense and absorbing for 30 minutes solo) needs a consequence that is felt at body scale.

**Index wording, reconciled.** The index bullet reads: "Segment-rig horrors with creep/unfold/snap behaviours, real occlusion and shadow; writes hidden-entity footprints (branching rime, radial hairlines, light disturbance) into the Graph footprint channel and submits light-disturbance modifiers to Lighting. MVP: one behaviour." This GDD honours every clause but one, and says so. *Segment-rig, creep / unfold / snap, one behaviour*: HE-1, HE-14, HE-15 (one cycle of one type; creep is LURK/STALK/RETREAT, unfold is REACH, snap is STRIKE). *Footprints into the Graph footprint channel*: the **physical half** (CHILL, hull-only GOUGE, RUPTURE) goes through M17; the **web-grammar half** (smear, branching rime, radial hairlines) is Horror's own persisted mark ring, because Failure & Trail draws only Graph descriptors (FT-31) and the Graph has no mark record (HE-27). *Light-disturbance modifiers to Lighting*: published state that Lighting reads, never a call (KRN:117; HE-35). *"Real occlusion and shadow"* is **read as visual opacity by draw order plus locomotion against Layout solids, and is not a `LightOccluder2D`, a shadow or an emission**: three designed GDDs (EM-20 (c), LO rail 10, FT-31) and the art bible's own recommendation (ART:296) rule the opposite, and a horror shadow would destroy the free stage-2 falsifier "a shadow with no occluder" (HE-2; orchestrator ruling R1). The index bullet, the routed thread, the art bible's "Physical honesty" bullet (ART:542) and PIPE:140 are listed as owed wording refreshes in Cross-References and are not edited here. **Until those rows land the art bible and this GDD contradict each other on the horror shadow, so the refresh rows (ART:542, ART 5.5, PIPE:140, IDX:35) are a BLOCKING precondition of `/asset-spec system:horror-entities` for the rig, exactly as C-HE-21 is for rime and hairlines (AC-HE-123); they are not advisory.** The creative-director affirmed the ruling at the CD-GDD-ALIGN gate (R1).

**Status of neighbours at authoring time (2026-10-26/27).** Designed and locked: Command & Simulation Layer, Life-Support Graph, Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera, Player Controller & Input; designed in this run: Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query, Attention System, 2D Lighting & Occlusion, Failure & Trail System, Item & Module Database, Suit & Equipment, Interaction, Ship Body & Interior Physics, Ship Section & Layout Data Model, Save/Load & Versioned Format, Derelict Authoring. Modular Ship Assembly and Sanity & Hallucination Rules are also designed in this run (`Status: Designed`); Web Map & Transit and Boarding & Salvage are `Status: Designed` on disk (Web Map was a draft at first authoring). Perception Filter, Adaptive Audio & Tells, HUD & Suit Layer, In-World Instruments, Chart Table and Debug Overlay were undesigned at first authoring and are all `Status: Designed` now; only Depth Rings & Scarcity, Knowledge Codex and Co-op have no GDD, and every assumption about those is marked `(provisional — <dep> undesigned)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Engine reference: `docs/engine-reference/godot/` has no `scripting.md` or `core.md` and no 2D-skeleton coverage in `animation.md`; GDScript operation cost and per-instance shader parameters are spike parameters, not sourced facts. **Refresh at the design review (2026-10-27):** every neighbour above now has a GDD with `Status: Designed` on disk, including Perception Filter, Web Map & Transit, Adaptive Audio & Tells, HUD & Suit Layer, In-World Instruments, Chart Table and the Debug Overlay; only Depth Rings & Scarcity, Knowledge Codex and Co-op have no file. The reads this GDD had marked provisional now exist under these names: `hull_segments_near(section_id, px, r)` and `behind_wall_footprint(section_id, px)` (Layout), `version(section_id)` for door-cache keys (Layout, LY-33), `emitters_near(body_id, px, r)` (Emitter), `loco_state` (Controller) and the five-tick alpha (Pipeline, line 204); the dead-end lint is registered as `DEAD_END_NARROW` (Derelict Authoring, `content_lint_ids`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. 1287	## Game Feel
1288	
1289	Horror has **no input of its own**: the player never presses anything at it (PC-12, HE-38). Its "feel" is the feel of being *read* by something patient and then *choosing* inside a window the design guarantees is long enough. The targets below therefore specify the **input-to-feedback chain** (what the player does in answer to what the horror shows), the **timing of the picture** (ticks, pose counts, px) and the **absence of every action-game punctuation** (hit-stop, shake, flash), each as a number. Conversions: 1 tick = 16.7 ms at `TICK_RATE` 60; one Horror run = 5 ticks = 83.3 ms = one 12 fps rig pose; 95 ticks = 1.58 s; 180 ticks = 3.00 s; 300 ticks = 5.00 s. Every number is `[PLACEHOLDER]` pending the blind-legibility playtest (AC-HE-106) and cites its Tuning Knob or Formula.
1290	
1291	### Feel Reference
1292	
1293	- **Adopt: the fixed-point telegraph of boss-style area attacks (Souls-like ground strikes, platformer stomps).** A long, readable wind-up whose *area is locked at its start*, so that moving out always works and a hit is the player's own stillness. Borrowed quality: **committed, heavy, fair.** The horror's snap is the only fast thing in its vocabulary, and it lands on a place the player was shown for one to three seconds (HE-14, HE-F5).
1294	- **Adopt: *Alien: Isolation*'s one persistent, physically present body** (a true position, never despawned) **and *Darkwood*'s light that attracts and marks that carry the past** (HE-13, HE-30). Borrowed quality: weather with intent, not a monster with a personality.
1295	- **Adopt in spirit: *Project Zomboid*'s "death is final and common"** (the user's decision), bounded to three told strikes; and *Amnesia*'s "you cannot fight it, only hide" (no attack input).
1296	- **Anti-reference (reject precisely):** *Alien: Isolation*'s director-driven menace gauge and grab-instakill (a hidden number and an unreadable death); any action-game hit-stop, screen shake, damage number or red flash (HE-38, the camera refuses horror callers); a stinger that scales with distance (a meter by ear, Pillar 3). **It must not feel** like a jump-scare machine, a boss with a health bar, or a creature that "locks on" and follows you (validation target 4).
1297	
1298	### Input Responsiveness
1299	
1300	The only inputs in the chain belong to the player (walk, lamp, door, pod) and to the sim (the horror's run). The budget is the **walk-out window** of HE-F5: from the limb entering the cone to the seat standing on the disc boundary, the player gets `UNFOLD_LO` 95 ticks, of which 54 are the assumed reaction allowance, 1 the kernel's command application and 37 the walk on the slowest (diagonal) octant (`t_out_max(V_WALK)`, HE-F2; 36 on a cardinal octant), leaving **3 ticks (50 ms) of slack** at the shortest draw (4 on a cardinal octant), which is also the whole allowance for input and display latency (`INPUT_LATENCY_TICKS`, unmeasured, HE-F5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
1301	
1302	| Action or cause | Max latency to visible or audible response | Frame budget (60 fps) | Notes |
1303	|---|---|---|---|
1304	| Attention's phase edge on a non-run tick to Horror acting on it | 4 ticks (67 ms) | 4 | Horror reads `attention.view` as committed by Attention's last run and acts at its next run (HE-4, E-HE-17); it only ever *lengthens* the warning |
1305	| Horror state change (REACH begin, STRIKE, RETREAT) to the rig pose on screen | 1 tick (17 ms) after the run that made it | 1 | The pose is a function of `(state, state_enter_T, now)`; the run that commits `locked_pt` and `reach_end_T` is the run whose pose the presenter draws |
1306	| Player's walk command to the seat moving | 1 tick (17 ms) | 1 | Kernel command application at `apply_tick >= T + 1` (KRN D.4); counted inside the 95-tick budget |
1307	| Player switches the lamp off to the horror's *next-run* target changing | 5 ticks (83 ms) | 5 | Target recomputed each run (HE-13); an **in-flight REACH is unaffected** (P is locked, E-HE-23) |
1308	| `strike_T` to the positional strike cue starting | 1 tick (17 ms) | 1 | A requirement on Adaptive Audio (Designed, `adaptive-audio-and-tells.md`, AA-28 c); the cue is the witness of strike one (HE-15) |
1309	| Strike to Suit's rung change and the Controller's stagger | at the next `suit.vitals` run, at most 6 ticks (100 ms) after the hit, with no hold (SE-23, `SUIT_EXO_BYPASS_LIMITER` 1); the Controller's stagger follows on the cap falling edge it reads after `suit.vitals` (PC-9) | <= 6 | Suit's and the Controller's; stagger lasts `STAGGER_TICKS` 30 (500 ms) |
1310	| Closing a door leaf to the strike no longer reaching through it | the same tick | 0 | The room test and the closed-leaf test are evaluated at resolution (HE-19) |
1311	
1312	### Animation Feel Targets
1313	
1314	"Startup" is the telegraph before the act has any effect; "Active" is the committed window in which the act is fixed and nothing the player does changes where it lands; "Recovery" is the horror's committed, vulnerable-in-the-world time (it is never vulnerable to the player; recovery is the player's **breathing room**). One pose = 5 ticks. All counts follow `UNFOLD_TICKS` in [95, 180] (19 to 36 poses).
1315	
1316	| Animation | Startup (ticks, poses) | Active (ticks, poses) | Recovery (ticks, poses) | Feel goal | Notes |
1317	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
1318	| **REACH** (enter + unfold + hold) | enter ~15 %: 15 to 27 (3 to 5); unfold ~55 %: 50 to 100 (10 to 20) | hold ~30 %, never under 30 ticks: 30 to 54 (6 to 11); **the tip does not move** | resolves into the snap | Committed, deliberate, readable: a heavy thing placing a limb | The limb enters the cone before the body; no icon, ring or decal; `reach_a/b/c` poses (V3, V4) |
1319	| **STRIKE** (snap) | 0 (no wind-up beyond the unfold) | 1 pose = 5 ticks (83 ms), then held for `STRIKE_HOLD_RUNS` 2 = 10 ticks (167 ms) | RETREAT begins at the end of the hold | Crisp and binary: the only fast motion Horror owns | No lunge travel, afterimage or trail (HE-24); the touch-down smear and the positional cue are the punctuation |
1320	| **REACH fizzle** | n/a | the reverse of the unfold poses over the same stage lengths | none; the cooldown is not consumed | Identical to a deliberate withdrawal, so a harmless hold cannot be told from a harmful one | The hold itself is always honest (V5) |
1321	| **RETREAT** | 0 | creep at `V_CREEP_MPX` 1000: 5 px per run; 96 ticks out to a nominal waypoint at 192 px | `STRIKE_COOLDOWN_TICKS` 300 (5.0 s) before STALK may resume; 65 ticks back at `V_HUNT_MPX` | A retreat reads as a retreat, not a hover (`t_out` 96 is inside the cooldown, HE-F15) | The realised period of a seat that does not move is 460 to 545 ticks (7.7 to 9.1 s); the earliest next strike is 395 ticks (6.6 s) after the last |
1322	| **Creep** (LURK, STALK in a TELL) | n/a | 1 px per tick, a pose per run, hash-irregular limb choice, no repeated configuration in consecutive steps | n/a | Patient, wet, structural; never a metronome (not the tell's beat), never a jitter | Dwell 900 ticks (15 s) at a LURK waypoint |
1323	| **Hunt** (STALK in BREACH) | n/a | 1.5 px per tick on average (7 then 8 px per run); a walker gains 0.5 px per tick on it | n/a | Inevitable but outwalkable: pressure, not a chase | `V_HUNT_MPX` below `V_WALK × 1000` is the escape invariant (HE-F6) |
1324	| **Ingress** | the ingress mark is laid 60 ticks (1.0 s) before the body | the rig emerges across the wall footprint's south edge; alpha is 0 or 255 | n/a | A body crossing a light boundary, never a fade | At least 300 ticks (5.0 s) of published stalk remain before the shortest tell ends (HE-F9) |
1325	| **Mark lay-down** | 3 frames (smear, rime) or 2 (hairlines), 5 ticks each | hold on the last lay-down frame (stage 0) | aged frames at stage 1 from age 6000 ticks and stage 2 from age 12000 ticks (thirds of `MARK_LIFE_TICKS` 18000) | A floor that remembers, readable as wet, tacky, dry | Frame swaps on a binary-alpha sprite; no fade |
1326	
1327	### Impact Moments
1328	
1329	Every row is **0 by design** (HE-38, the anti-pillar "not a combat game"; the camera refuses a Horror-tagged caller). The punctuation the strike *does* carry is listed after the table. "Configurable?" is **No** for every row: these are lint failures, not tuning options.
1330	
1331	| Impact type | Duration | Effect | Configurable? |
1332	|---|---|---|---|
1333	| Hit-stop (freeze frames) | 0 ms | none | No (HE-38; AC-HE-72, AC-HE-116) |
1334	| Screen shake | 0 ms | none | No (PIPE C1, C9; the jolt API refuses a Horror-tagged caller) |
1335	| Camera impact or zoom punch | 0 ms | none | No (the camera never reacts to a horror) |
1336	| Hit flash, vignette, chromatic aberration | 0 ms | none | No (Visual/Audio: forbidden feedback) |
1337	| Damage number, health pip, threat bar | n/a | none | No (HE-38) |
1338	| Controller rumble | none from Horror | Neither the Player Controller & Input GDD nor Suit & Equipment defines a rumble rule; if one is added for the stagger or the CRITICAL rung it is theirs (HUD & Suit Layer: designed (`hud-and-suit-layer.md`)) | No (not Horror's) |
1339	| Time-scale slowdown | 0 ms | none | No |
1340	
1341	**The punctuation the strike does carry:** the single **snap pose** (5 ticks, then a 10-tick hold), the **touch-down smear** laid at the point 25 to 50 ticks earlier, at the start of the hold stage, and still on the floor, **Audio's positional cue** starting within 1 tick of `strike_T`, the **STRUCK burst** laid at P only when a seat was hit (a miss leaves the smear alone), and **Suit's own consequence** (the rung, the stagger, from strike two the seam jet). Strike one has no persistent witness on the body (Suit's STRAINED rung is inert by design, SE:83); the strike and the STRUCK mark on the floor are the witness, which is why those things exist (HE-15, C-HE-25).
1342	
1343	### Weight and Responsiveness Profile
1344	
1345	- **Weight.** Heavy and deliberate. The horror is slower than the walker (1.0 to 1.5 px per tick against 2), roots its body for the whole telegraph and resolves in one step. It never hurries, never poses and never roars.
1346	- **Player control.** High at every moment until the commit. The strike point is locked, so *moving out of the disc always works*; the player can course-correct for the whole telegraph and, because there is no tracking, cannot be "chased" into a hit. Control ends only for a carrier (`V_CARRY` 1 needs 72 ticks, 73 diagonal, against 40 available, so a carrier who keeps the cargo is struck on 7 of 18 draws; the answer is to drop the cargo) and for a seat that stands still.
1347	- **Snap quality.** The creep and unfold are stepped at 12 fps with smoothed position (analogue in motion, discrete in pose); the strike is a **binary one-step snap**. The contrast between the long stillness of the hold and the single step of the snap is the whole read.
1348	- **Acceleration model.** Simulation feel, no ramp: speed is a constant cadence (`v_eff` per tick from the accumulator, HE-F6), and a speed change at a phase edge is instantaneous in the sim and invisible as acceleration on screen (position is interpolated, pose is stepped). There is no lunge momentum and no overshoot.
1349	- **Failure texture.** Fair, never random: the player was shown the limb, the stillness and the smear, and a hit reads as "I stood there" or "I was carrying". The target is that **at least 80 % of horror-caused deaths are described with a cause the player saw** (validation target 1). There is nothing hidden: no stored aggro, no lock-on, no number. Dying is lethal (user decision), restores from the newest autosave, and shows no death screen or beat (SL-7).
1350	
1351	### Feel Acceptance Criteria
1352	
1353	Subjective targets stated precisely enough to get consistent verdicts; the manual rows that measure them are the numbered criteria in Acceptance Criteria Group M, and the sample rule (N >= 10) applies.
1354	
1355	- [ ] Playtesters describe the telegraph as "it was aiming at that spot" or equivalent for at least 87.5 % of first-time players (7 of 8 equivalent, N >= 10; AC-HE-106); none uses "cheap", "unfair" or "came out of nowhere" unprompted for a *told* strike.
1356	- [ ] Of the players who were hit, at least 75 % call it avoidable (AC-HE-106); at least 80 % of horror-caused deaths are described with a cause the player saw (AC-HE-116).
1357	- [ ] The unfold-hold-snap sequence reads at k = 1, `k_auto` and `k_auto + 2` as "limb extended, tip on a tile" (at k = 1 only "limb extended") (AC-HE-107).
1358	- [ ] The creep reads as patient and irregular: no tester says "glitchy", "teleporting", "jittery" or "puppet" (AC-HE-108, AC-HE-117); pose changes land only on multiples of 5 ticks.
1359	- [ ] No tester reports a hit-stop, shake, flash or number from the horror (AC-HE-116), and none reports an unfair pop-in on ingress (AC-HE-112).
1360	- [ ] A player who reacts within the 54-tick allowance escapes at every legal draw of `UNFOLD_TICKS` (AC-HE-88); the 3-tick slack (4 on a cardinal octant) is felt as "just made it" at the shortest draw, never as "it hit me where I was not" *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
1361	- [ ] Zero testers describe the horror "remembering" or "locking on" across a lamp-off (validation target 4, AC-HE-115).
1362	- [ ] The breathing gap between a snap and the next limb (at least 365 ticks, 6.1 s, for a seat that stays in range) is described as a lull to act in, not as a long pause or a screech (AC-HE-115).
1363	- [ ] Reduced motion keeps the telegraph readable (AC-HE-113).
1364	
1365	## UI Requirements
1366	
1367	**Horror Entities has no UI of its own.** It owns no HUD element, no instrument, no chart-table row, no menu and no overlay, and it must not acquire one: Pillar 3 says the web's attention and its consequences are "shown in the world, never a meter", and the anti-pillar against a combat game rules out every standard enemy-awareness widget. Everything the player learns about a horror comes through the world: the rig in the beam, the marks on the floor, the dips on nearby lamps, Audio's positional facts, and Suit's and Failure & Trail's consequences. The surfaces that exist in the game and touch this system are owned elsewhere; this section states what each must **not** do and what Horror supplies. A UX spec is therefore not requested for Horror; the UX note at the end is a *negative* requirement routed to the HUD owner.
1368	
1369	| Information | Display location | Update frequency | Condition | Owner |
1370	|---|---|---|---|---|
1371	| Where a horror is, what state it is in, which seat it prefers, where its limb will land | **Nowhere in the HUD.** The player reads the rig, the limb tip and the touch-down smear in the world | n/a | never | Horror (world only) |
1372	| That a hit landed | The snap pose, Audio's positional cue and, afterwards, the STRUCK burst on the floor at P (a miss leaves only the touch-down smear) (HE-15); then Suit's own rung display and stagger | on the strike | a seat in the disc | Suit & Equipment, HUD & Suit Layer |
1373	| Suit integrity after strikes | Suit's existing instrument or HUD row (STRAINED is inert and carries no witness by design, SE:83; CRITICAL shows the leak, seam jet and stagger) | Suit's | Suit's | Suit & Equipment, HUD & Suit Layer |
1374	| The ship's hull damage from a GOUGE or RUPTURE | Failure & Trail's hull descriptor and the Graph's own instruments | the Graph's | a hull act | Failure & Trail, In-World Instruments |
1375	| That the lamp is on or off (the horror's target rule) | Controller and Suit's lamp state; the lit-only verb gating | immediate | always | Player Controller, Interaction |
1376	| Where it has been | the marks themselves (smear, rime, hairlines), never a map pin, trail overlay or "last seen" marker on the Chart Table or Web Map | n/a | never | Horror (world only); Chart Table, Web Map must not add one |
1377	| True horror positions, target, state, locked point, budgets and counters | **Debug Overlay (True Values), development builds only** | per run | developer flag | Debug Overlay (`horror.view` is read-only); never exposed as an accessibility feature |
1378	| Save status | Save/Load's pause-panel and failed-write notice, unrelated to Horror | Save/Load's | Save/Load's | Save/Load |
1379	
1380	**Rules for the surfaces that exist (negative requirements, each an acceptance criterion).**
1381	- No HUD, instrument, chart-table or web-map element shows a horror, a threat bar, a proximity indicator, a direction, an off-screen arrow, a countdown to a strike, a "last seen" pin or a target ring, **under any accessibility setting** (Pillar 3, AT-24; AC-HE-119).
1382	- No audio-to-visual accessibility feature may name, point to or time a horror (a captioned cue such as "something nearby" is a proximity indicator by another name). The accessibility mapping for Horror's audio facts is an Open Question for the accessibility specialist and the HUD owner, with the constraint that it never reveals position, state or direction.
1383	- No cursor, reticle or interaction prompt appears on a horror: HORROR subjects take no verb and any forced command is `INVALID_TARGET` (IA-39, AC-IA-113).
1384	- The Debug Overlay's true-value drawing is a development tool; a shipping build cannot enable it.
1385	- Accessibility options that change Horror's presentation (reduced motion, reduced flashing, ambient-floor reveal) act on the world drawing described in Visual/Audio Requirements and never add a surface (the ambient-floor option reveals hull only, never a horror or a mark).
1386	
1387	**UX note (deliberately not a UX flag).** This system has **no UI of its own**, so no `/ux-design` pass is requested for it. The HUD & Suit Layer (designed (`hud-and-suit-layer.md`)), In-World Instruments, Chart Table and Debug Overlay (designed (`debug-overlay-true-values.md`)) UX specs must repeat the negative requirements above and list "no horror element" in their own acceptance criteria; the HUD state list in AC-HE-119 is finalised from the HUD UX spec. `(provisional — In-World Instruments and Chart Table UX specs)`.

The registry carries the alias note, but this GDD says 'the kernel's one derivation `threat_counter`' and gates on it. AC-HE-136 (cases i-iii) still says 'read NOT ASSESSED until Save/Load and the kernel publish `kernel.clock.restore_epoch` and `threat_counter`'. OQ 29 gates slice 1 on 'the kernel publishing `threat_counter`' and OQ 31 lists 'owed by the kernel: the derivation'. Both have already been published, as `rng_derive_epoch` plus the `kernel.clock` view. Taken literally, the rows can never leave NOT ASSESSED, and the NOT ASSESSED rule says that blocks story closure.
findings.fix: Say once, in HE-42, that Horror calls the kernel's `rng_derive_epoch(world_seed, "horror.tell", counter)`, with `threat_counter` retained only as 'Horror's local name for counter_eff' (matching the registry alias). Replace 'threat_counter' with 'rng_derive_epoch' in AC-HE-24, 80, 82, 136, the knob-source row, Cross-References and OQ 29/31. Rewrite the AC-HE-136 gate to: cases (i)-(iii) run against the real slot_epoch.bin staging step and read NOT ASSESSED only if SL-23 / KRN-EPO-04 are not yet implemented. Mark OQ 29 and 31 owed-by-kernel as done.

findings.section: HE-14 / Visual-Audio V4 and stage table / Game Feel REACH row / AC-HE-26, 106, 143 (unresolved since 2026-10-28)
findings.finding: The hold stage has two definitions. The sim (HE-14 and AC-HE-143) gives hold_start_T = reach_end_T - 5 x floor(3n/10), which is 25 to 50 ticks (5 to 10 poses). The art table and Game Feel give 'last ~30 %, never under 30 ticks: 30 to 54 (6 to 11 poses)', and V4 lays the touch-down SMEAR 'on the first pose step of this stage'. At n = 19 the rig's hold starts one run before the sim lays the smear. AC-HE-26 asserts that the smear is absent before hold_start_T and the limb tip is already at rest, so the pose-tag test and the mark test disagree on the same frame.
findings.fix: Make the sim authoritative. Rewrite V4, the stage table row (c), the Game Feel REACH row and the Hold-stage Gaps bullet to '25 to 50 ticks (5 to 10 poses), starting at hold_start_T'. Drive the presenter's hold pose from `horror.view` (reach_end_T minus hold_start_T) rather than from its own 30 % share.

findings.section: AC-HE-17, HE-11, HE-35, HE-F11, HE-42 (partly resolved since 2026-10-28)
findings.finding: HE-11 now hashes `he_hash(entity_id, dwell_index, anchor_local_key, SALT_WP)`. AC-HE-17 still asserts 'the lowest `hash(entity_id, dwell_index, HE_HASH_SEED)`', which has no per-candidate term, so every candidate ties and the waypoint order is undefined. `anchor_local_key` is never defined. Layout anchors are keyed per section, and a body can hold several sections. `run_n` (HE-35, HE-F11, AC-HE-139) is also never defined. If an implementer makes it a counter, AC-HE-76's manifest check fails. If it is derived from T, nothing says so.
findings.fix: Define `anchor_local_key = (section_id << 16) | anchor_index`, using Layout's stable anchor ordering, or whatever unique key Layout publishes. Define `run_n = T div 5` (the Horror run index, derived and not persisted). Rewrite AC-HE-17 as: 'the next waypoint is the argmin over candidates of he_hash(entity_id, dwell_index, anchor_local_key, SALT_WP), ties lowest key; the fixture pins he_hash(7, 3, 0, SALT_WP) = 0x42973A88C2EF0EA3 from AC-HE-139 and one multi-section body.'

findings.section: HE-F9, HE-20, AC-HE-44, AC-HE-125 (unresolved since 2026-10-28)
findings.finding: The ingress relation has zero slack (300 + 240 + 60 = 600 = TELL_MIN_TICKS). arrive_T is the first Horror run on the 5-grid at or after fallback_T + lead. With a TELL entry at T mod 5 != 0 (Attention runs on a 6-tick grid) and tell_len = 600, the fallback body registers up to 4 ticks after BREACH entry. AC-HE-44 asserts 'registers by 600 ... clear before BREACH entry' on an unpinned fixture and treats the opposite as a build-failing cry-wolf defect. AC-HE-125 pins T mod 5 = 0 and admits the 4 ticks, so the two rows disagree.
findings.fix: Either tighten the relation to INGRESS_DELAY + STALK_VISIBLE_FLOOR + INGRESS_MARK_LEAD <= TELL_MIN_TICKS - (HORROR_RUN_TICKS - 1) (so the defaults become 300 / 220 / 60), or scope AC-HE-44 to 'by the first Horror run at or after tell_enter_T + 600' and define the cry-wolf defect as ingress pending at the first Horror run in BREACH. Update AC-HE-42 and AC-HE-90's negative fixtures accordingly.

findings.section: HE-26 door-eject, HE-43, AC-HE-104, AC-HE-137 (partly resolved since 2026-10-28)
findings.finding: HE-26 now says the eject is 'at most four queries, inside the five-query budget'. Guard 4 runs before the run's own locomotion, and HE-43 and AC-HE-104 allow 5 `solid_in` queries per run, one per tick of movement. An eject run that also walks costs up to 9, so the claim only holds if the eject run takes no locomotion step. The text never says so.
findings.fix: State in HE-26 and guard 4 that a run in which the eject executes performs no locomotion step (or that the eject spends the queries of the steps it replaces). Add that case to AC-HE-137 and AC-HE-104 ('eject run: <= 5 solid_in queries in total').

findings.section: HE-13 goal commit, HE-26 held_at_leaf, HE-41 group 4, AC-HE-142
findings.finding: The goal is released when 'its seat leaves the candidate set', and `held_at_leaf` holds 'while that seat remains the target'. The target is deliberately not persisted, and HE-41 group 4 stores goal_wp, goal_room and goal_commit_runs but no seat id. A restore mid-commit cannot evaluate the release test, and AC-HE-142's 'target changing to a reachable lit seat' has no stored referent.
findings.fix: Define both tests on persisted data: release when the fresh target's goal room differs from the stored `goal_room`, or when the fresh target is ANCHOR and the goal was a seat. Alternatively persist `goal_seat` in group 4 and add it to the manifest and the RANGE and STATE_INCOHERENT checks. Mirror the choice in AC-HE-81 case (f) and (h).

findings.section: HE-26 leaf mark, HE-27 taxonomy, HE-30 quotas, Visual/Audio table (unresolved since 2026-10-28)

It shares `MARK_QUOTA_HAIRLINES` 3 with strike, GOUGE, RUPTURE, anchor, ingress and egress contacts, so a few camping edge-triggers evict the strike and hull hairlines, which are the truth channel. A leaf face is also a wall face, and OQ 23 says wall-face marks have no draw band.

Add it to the V-table and AC-HE-57, and state its eviction class. If it must stay HAIRLINES, raise the quota or exclude the leaf mark from the HAIRLINES count.

findings.section: HE-25, HE-19, E-HE-29, AC-HE-48 (unresolved since 2026-10-28)
findings.finding: E-HE-29 says 'it may path across the new join', but HE-25 builds its room graph from `room_adjacency(section_id)` per section. A welded HATCH record has room_b = EXTERIOR, and no published read pairs the two sides. Layout AC-180 gives both sections the same open_extent_px with gap rects that coincide after composing section_offset, but no GDD turns that into a pairing rule. As written, a horror cannot cross a weld seam, and `linked` and `connected` are undefined across sections.
findings.fix: Add to HE-25 an explicit pairing rule: two HATCH records form one edge iff their `door_passage` gap_rects, composed with `section_offset`, coincide and their sections are in the same body. Or raise a G6 GAP request to Layout for a `paired_hatch(section_id, via_id)` read. Add a welded-seam fixture to AC-HE-48 and AC-HE-51.

findings.section: Tuning Knobs HORROR_MARK_DRAW_GROUPS, AC-HE-100, C-HE-31, OQ 11 (unresolved since 2026-10-27)
findings.finding: The load assertion is HORROR_MARK_DRAW_GROUPS <= D_marks - TRAIL_DMARKS_SHARE, while the knob text says 'at 4..6 Horror gets none'. With default 4, any D_marks below 10 fails the load, so the graceful 'gets none' never happens. The note 'at D_marks <= 10 ... cannot both get their share' is off by one (at exactly 10 both fit). Pipeline OQ 17, F&T 26b and this GDD each defer the floor to the others, so C-HE-31 is a three-way deadlock and AC-HE-100 is NOT ASSESSED forever.
findings.fix: Decide it here as the owner of the knob. Make the knob effective = clamp(D_marks - TRAIL_DMARKS_SHARE, 0, HORROR_MARK_DRAW_GROUPS), asserted as an inequality that never fails the load. Adopt the proposed floor 'the newest HAIRLINES or STRUCK mark of the current epoch is always drawn'. Fix the '<= 10' text to '< 10'. Close C-HE-31 and give AC-HE-100 a concrete expected group count at D_marks 4, 6, 9 and 10.

findings.section: Tuning Knobs LURK_STANDOFF_PX safe range, HE-F9/F13/F14 tables (unresolved since 2026-10-28)

findings.section: AC-HE-106, AC-HE-107, Game Feel Acceptance line 1, AC-HE-120 (unresolved since 2026-10-27; untestable as written)

findings.section: Tuning Knobs UNFOLD_SCALE_PCT / HE-F5 / HE-41 (unresolved since 2026-10-27; third consecutive review)
findings.finding: `horror_set_unfold_scale(pct)` is specified as a command with `HOST` origin. Kernel CR-6 and CR-7 allow only PLAYER or SYSTEM origins, and the name appears in no other GDD (grep finds 0 in kernel, HUD, Controller and Save/Load). No settings surface can issue it. This is the GDD's own named fallback when the blind-legibility test (AC-HE-106) fails, and AC-HE-88 tests it at scale 150. Separately, the value lives in the WORLD-scoped `horror.state`, so a death restore rolls an accessibility setting back to its saved value and a new game resets it to 100.
findings.fix: Re-declare the command as `allowed_origins = {PLAYER}`, actor_binding NONE, issued by the HUD/settings owner (name that owner in Dependencies). Better still, hold the scale in a PROFILE-scoped setting that the Horror step reads through a kernel view. Record the setting owner and the origin in HE-F5 and the knob row, and rewrite the HE-41 clause 'changed only by the host command' to match. Keep the default of 100, which ships regardless.

findings.section: HE-14 / Visual-Audio V4 and stage table / Game Feel REACH row / AC-HE-26, 106, 143 (unresolved since 2026-10-28)

findings.section: AC-HE-17, HE-11, HE-35, HE-F11, HE-42 (partly resolved since 2026-10-28)
findings.finding: HE-11 now hashes `he_hash(entity_id, dwell_index, anchor_local_key, SALT_WP)`. findings.fix: Define `anchor_local_key = (section_id << 16) | anchor_index`, using Layout's stable anchor ordering, or whatever unique key Layout publishes. Define `run_n = T div 5` (the Horror run index, derived and not persisted). Rewrite AC-HE-17 as: 'the next waypoint is the argmin over candidates of he_hash(entity_id, dwell_index, anchor_local_key, SALT_WP), ties lowest key; the fixture pins he_hash(7, 3, 0, SALT_WP) = 0x42973A88C2EF0EA3 from AC-HE-139 and one multi-section body.'

findings.section: HE-F9, HE-20, AC-HE-44, AC-HE-125 (unresolved since 2026-10-28)
findings.finding: The ingress relation has zero slack (300 + 240 + 60 = 600 = TELL_MIN_TICKS). arrive_T is the first Horror run on the 5-grid at or after fallback_T + lead. With a TELL entry at T mod 5 != 0 (Attention runs on a 6-tick grid) and tell_len = 600, the fallback body registers up to 4 ticks after BREACH entry. AC-HE-44 asserts 'registers by 600 ... clear before BREACH entry' on an unpinned fixture and treats the opposite as a build-failing cry-wolf defect. AC-HE-125 pins T mod 5 = 0 and admits the 4 ticks, so the two rows disagree.
findings.fix: Either tighten the relation to INGRESS_DELAY + STALK_VISIBLE_FLOOR + INGRESS_MARK_LEAD <= TELL_MIN_TICKS - (HORROR_RUN_TICKS - 1) (so the defaults become 300 / 220 / 60), or scope AC-HE-44 to 'by the first Horror run at or after tell_enter_T + 600' and define the cry-wolf defect as ingress pending at the first Horror run in BREACH. Update AC-HE-42 and AC-HE-90's negative fixtures accordingly.

findings.section: HE-26 door-eject, HE-43, AC-HE-104, AC-HE-137 (partly resolved since 2026-10-28)
findings.finding: HE-26 now says the eject is 'at most four queries, inside the five-query budget'. Guard 4 runs before the run's own locomotion, and HE-43 and AC-HE-104 allow 5 `solid_in` queries per run, one per tick of movement. An eject run that also walks costs up to 9, so the claim only holds if the eject run takes no locomotion step. The text never says so.
findings.fix: State in HE-26 and guard 4 that a run in which the eject executes performs no locomotion step (or that the eject spends the queries of the steps it replaces). Add that case to AC-HE-137 and AC-HE-104 ('eject run: <= 5 solid_in queries in total').

findings.section: HE-13 goal commit, HE-26 held_at_leaf, HE-41 group 4, AC-HE-142
findings.finding: The goal is released when 'its seat leaves the candidate set', and `held_at_leaf` holds 'while that seat remains the target'. findings.section: HE-25, HE-19, E-HE-29, AC-HE-48 (unresolved since 2026-10-28)
findings.finding: E-HE-29 says 'it may path across the new join', but HE-25 builds its room graph from `room_adjacency(section_id)` per section. findings.section: Tuning Knobs HORROR_MARK_DRAW_GROUPS, AC-HE-100, C-HE-31, OQ 11 (unresolved since 2026-10-27)
findings.finding: The load assertion is HORROR_MARK_DRAW_GROUPS <= D_marks - TRAIL_DMARKS_SHARE, while the knob text says 'at 4..6 Horror gets none'. findings.fix: Say once, in HE-42, that Horror calls the kernel's `rng_derive_epoch(world_seed, "horror.tell", counter)`, with `threat_counter` retained only as 'Horror's local name for counter_eff' (matching the registry alias). Rewrite the AC-HE-136 gate to: cases (i)-(iii) run against the real slot_epoch.bin staging step and read NOT ASSESSED only if SL-23 / KRN-EPO-04 are not yet implemented. Mark OQ 29 and 31 owed-by-kernel as done.

findings.section: HE-14 / Visual-Audio V4 and stage table / Game Feel REACH row / AC-HE-26, 106, 143 (unresolved since 2026-10-28)
findings.finding: The hold stage has two definitions. The sim (HE-14 and AC-HE-143) gives hold_start_T = reach_end_T - 5 x floor(3n/10), which is 25 to 50 ticks (5 to 10 poses). The art table and Game Feel give 'last ~30 %, never under 30 ticks: 30 to 54 (6 to 11 poses)', and V4 lays the touch-down SMEAR 'on the first pose step of this stage'. At n = 19 the rig's hold starts one run before the sim lays the smear. AC-HE-26 asserts that the smear is absent before hold_start_T and the limb tip is already at rest, so the pose-tag test and the mark test disagree on the same frame.
findings.fix: Make the sim authoritative. Rewrite V4, the stage table row (c), the Game Feel REACH row and the Hold-stage Gaps bullet to '25 to 50 ticks (5 to 10 poses), starting at hold_start_T'. Drive the presenter's hold pose from `horror.view` (reach_end_T minus hold_start_T) rather than from its own 30 % share.

findings.section: AC-HE-17, HE-11, HE-35, HE-F11, HE-42 (partly resolved since 2026-10-28)
findings.finding: HE-11 now hashes `he_hash(entity_id, dwell_index, anchor_local_key, SALT_WP)`. AC-HE-17 still asserts 'the lowest `hash(entity_id, dwell_index, HE_HASH_SEED)`', which has no per-candidate term, so every candidate ties and the waypoint order is undefined. `anchor_local_key` is never defined. Layout anchors are keyed per section, and a body can hold several sections. `run_n` (HE-35, HE-F11, AC-HE-139) is also never defined. If an implementer makes it a counter, AC-HE-76's manifest check fails. If it is derived from T, nothing says so.
findings.fix: Define `anchor_local_key = (section_id << 16) | anchor_index`, using Layout's stable anchor ordering, or whatever unique key Layout publishes. Define `run_n = T div 5` (the Horror run index, derived and not persisted). Rewrite AC-HE-17 as: 'the next waypoint is the argmin over candidates of he_hash(entity_id, dwell_index, anchor_local_key, SALT_WP), ties lowest key; the fixture pins he_hash(7, 3, 0, SALT_WP) = 0x42973A88C2EF0EA3 from AC-HE-139 and one multi-section body.'

findings.section: HE-F9, HE-20, AC-HE-44, AC-HE-125 (unresolved since 2026-10-28)
findings.finding: The ingress relation has zero slack (300 + 240 + 60 = 600 = TELL_MIN_TICKS). arrive_T is the first Horror run on the 5-grid at or after fallback_T + lead. With a TELL entry at T mod 5 != 0 (Attention runs on a 6-tick grid) and tell_len = 600, the fallback body registers up to 4 ticks after BREACH entry. AC-HE-44 asserts 'registers by 600 ... clear before BREACH entry' on an unpinned fixture and treats the opposite as a build-failing cry-wolf defect. AC-HE-125 pins T mod 5 = 0 and admits the 4 ticks, so the two rows disagree.
findings.fix: Either tighten the relation to INGRESS_DELAY + STALK_VISIBLE_FLOOR + INGRESS_MARK_LEAD <= TELL_MIN_TICKS - (HORROR_RUN_TICKS - 1) (so the defaults become 300 / 220 / 60), or scope AC-HE-44 to 'by the first Horror run at or after tell_enter_T + 600' and define the cry-wolf defect as ingress pending at the first Horror run in BREACH. Update AC-HE-42 and AC-HE-90's negative fixtures accordingly.

findings.section: HE-26 door-eject, HE-43, AC-HE-104, AC-HE-137 (partly resolved since 2026-10-28)
findings.finding: HE-26 now says the eject is 'at most four queries, inside the five-query budget'. Guard 4 runs before the run's own locomotion, and HE-43 and AC-HE-104 allow 5 `solid_in` queries per run, one per tick of movement. An eject run that also walks costs up to 9, so the claim only holds if the eject run takes no locomotion step. The text never says so.
findings.fix: State in HE-26 and guard 4 that a run in which the eject executes performs no locomotion step (or that the eject spends the queries of the steps it replaces). Add that case to AC-HE-137 and AC-HE-104 ('eject run: <= 5 solid_in queries in total').

findings.section: HE-13 goal commit, HE-26 held_at_leaf, HE-41 group 4, AC-HE-142
findings.finding: The goal is released when 'its seat leaves the candidate set', and `held_at_leaf` holds 'while that seat remains the target'. The target is deliberately not persisted, and HE-41 group 4 stores goal_wp, goal_room and goal_commit_runs but no seat id. A restore mid-commit cannot evaluate the release test, and AC-HE-142's 'target changing to a reachable lit seat' has no stored referent.
findings.fix: Define both tests on persisted data: release when the fresh target's goal room differs from the stored `goal_room`, or when the fresh target is ANCHOR and the goal was a seat. Alternatively persist `goal_seat` in group 4 and add it to the manifest and the RANGE and STATE_INCOHERENT checks. Mirror the choice in AC-HE-81 case (f) and (h).

findings.section: HE-26 leaf mark, HE-27 taxonomy, HE-30 quotas, Visual/Audio table (unresolved since 2026-10-28)
findings.finding: The HAIRLINES mark laid on a leaf face when the horror camps at a closed door (`horror_leaf_marks`) is absent from the HE-27 taxonomy, the HE-30 production list and priority, and the Visual/Audio mark table. It has no draw band. It shares `MARK_QUOTA_HAIRLINES` 3 with strike, GOUGE, RUPTURE, anchor, ingress and egress contacts, so a few camping edge-triggers evict the strike and hull hairlines, which are the truth channel. A leaf face is also a wall face, and OQ 23 says wall-face marks have no draw band.
findings.fix: Add the leaf mark to HE-27 and HE-30 with its own kind (for example LEAF) and quota, or lay it as a floor mark at the sill in the existing floor-marks band. Add it to the V-table and AC-HE-57, and state its eviction class. If it must stay HAIRLINES, raise the quota or exclude the leaf mark from the HAIRLINES count.

findings.section: HE-25, HE-19, E-HE-29, AC-HE-48 (unresolved since 2026-10-28)
findings.finding: E-HE-29 says 'it may path across the new join', but HE-25 builds its room graph from `room_adjacency(section_id)` per section. A welded HATCH record has room_b = EXTERIOR, and no published read pairs the two sides. Layout AC-180 gives both sections the same open_extent_px with gap rects that coincide after composing section_offset, but no GDD turns that into a pairing rule. As written, a horror cannot cross a weld seam, and `linked` and `connected` are undefined across sections.
findings.fix: Add to HE-25 an explicit pairing rule: two HATCH records form one edge iff their `door_passage` gap_rects, composed with `section_offset`, coincide and their sections are in the same body. Or raise a G6 GAP request to Layout for a `paired_hatch(section_id, via_id)` read. Add a welded-seam fixture to AC-HE-48 and AC-HE-51.

findings.section: Tuning Knobs HORROR_MARK_DRAW_GROUPS, AC-HE-100, C-HE-31, OQ 11 (unresolved since 2026-10-27)
findings.finding: The load assertion is HORROR_MARK_DRAW_GROUPS <= D_marks - TRAIL_DMARKS_SHARE, while the knob text says 'at 4..6 Horror gets none'. With default 4, any D_marks below 10 fails the load, so the graceful 'gets none' never happens. The note 'at D_marks <= 10 ... cannot both get their share' is off by one (at exactly 10 both fit). Pipeline OQ 17, F&T 26b and this GDD each defer the floor to the others, so C-HE-31 is a three-way deadlock and AC-HE-100 is NOT ASSESSED forever.
findings.fix: Decide it here as the owner of the knob. Make the knob effective = clamp(D_marks - TRAIL_DMARKS_SHARE, 0, HORROR_MARK_DRAW_GROUPS), asserted as an inequality that never fails the load. Adopt the proposed floor 'the newest HAIRLINES or STRUCK mark of the current epoch is always drawn'. Fix the '<= 10' text to '< 10'. Close C-HE-31 and give AC-HE-100 a concrete expected group count at D_marks 4, 6, 9 and 10.

findings.section: Tuning Knobs LURK_STANDOFF_PX safe range, HE-F9/F13/F14 tables (unresolved since 2026-10-28)
findings.finding: The safe range is stated as 144..288 in four places. The knob row itself says Sanity's boot assertion `HIDE_SAFE_R (288) > LURK_STANDOFF_PX` makes Sanity refuse to boot at 288, so the top of the 'safe' range is not safe.
findings.fix: Change the range to 144..287 (or 144..HIDE_SAFE_R - 1) in the knob row, HE-F9, HE-F13 and HE-F14 tables, and the registry range.

findings.section: AC-HE-106, AC-HE-107, Game Feel Acceptance line 1, AC-HE-120 (unresolved since 2026-10-27; untestable as written)
findings.finding: Four acceptance rows cannot be passed or failed as written. AC-HE-107: 'at least 90 % of 5 blind judges' (4.5 judges). AC-HE-106: 'in all five facings' (the rig has no facings; AC-HE-107 uses 8 aim directions). Game Feel line 1: 'at least 87.5 % ... (7 of 8 equivalent, N >= 10)' contradicts AC-HE-106's ceil(0.875 x N) (9 of 10). AC-HE-120: 'The exemption is checked by review' gives no pass condition.
findings.fix: AC-HE-107: 'at least 5 of 5 blind judges (or 4 of 5 with a recorded dissent)'. A cleaner alternative is N >= 10 judges and at least ceil(0.9 x N). AC-HE-106: drop 'in all five facings'; require 'in every capture of the 8 aim directions at k = 1, k_auto and k_auto + 2 (24 of 24, AC-HE-107)'. Game Feel line 1: 'at least ceil(0.875 x N) first-time players (9 of 10), N >= 10; AC-HE-106'. AC-HE-120: 'every whitelist entry carries a file, line and reason, and the scan fails if a whitelisted line no longer exists or an entry lacks a reason'; delete the review clause.

findings.section: AC-HE-133, E-HE-56, AC-HE-94 (unresolved since 2026-10-28)
findings.finding: The decompression deadline is cited as 'about 131 s = 7860 ticks at the initial hole, LSG:707, a figure to be re-cited on the confirming run'. The re-cite marker is still there. The Graph's BREACH-EVENT row (line 775 now, not 707) reads 131 s at the initial hole and 105-120 s with the stressed fatigue that a RUPTURE sets. The relevant clock for the CRITICAL walk-only seat is therefore about 105 s, i.e. about 12 600 px at V_WALK. The 'about 15 000 px' figure and the 7860-tick deadline are too generous.
findings.fix: Cite the band: 'decompression 131 s at the initial hole, 105 to 120 s once the stressed fatigue grows it (LSG D.15 BREACH-EVENT)'. Use 105 s (6300 ticks, about 12 600 px) as the AC-HE-133 bound, or have the AC read the Graph's published `failures()` threshold only, as it already says it does. Drop the 're-cite' marker and update the stale line number.

findings.section: Tuning Knobs / Dependencies: SUIT_PATCH_CAP_BP range, HE-F3, OQ 34, C-HE-36 (unresolved since 2026-10-28)
findings.finding: Suit and the registry still register SUIT_PATCH_CAP_BP range 5100..6900, but HE-F3's third bound needs cap >= STRIKE_BP + SUIT_HP_FAIL (5700 at the default). The only guard is a data-load rejection of the pairing. This is the third-pass-open ask to Suit, with no owner action.

findings.section: Open Question 4 / C-HE-21 / HE-31 Rime White-Grey (unresolved since 2026-10-28)

findings.section: Interactions / Dependencies 'verbatim' neighbour quotes and line cites
findings.finding: The Interactions tables call their quotes 'the neighbour's own row (verbatim)', but most are stale. Attention's row is quoted as '(no file; stage directory empty - provisional)' at AT:373, while the live row is at AT:390 and reads '(designed, horror-entities.md)'. findings.section: Cross-GDD sync: Boarding & Salvage ASK-BS-H1 / OQ-BS-33 and Derelict Authoring
findings.finding: HE-26, E-HE-59, the Interactions rows, C-HE-8 and OQ 7 say Boarding's ASK-BS-H1 / OQ-BS-33 is 'answered by the owner': a horror may path in `a_spine`, with no bypass and the spine not widened. Boarding still lists both as open ('Counterpart requested ... no counterpart text exists yet'). Derelict Authoring has no a_spine / horror text. The answer therefore exists in one file only. Bidirectionality for this ruling is not satisfied, and DA's lint for a 3-wide spine (it sits exactly at the 144 px floor of the E-HE-26 dead-end lint) is unconfirmed.
findings.fix: Queue edits for the Boarding writer (BS-13, EC-BS-26, ASK-BS-H1, OQ-BS-33 to 'Resolved 2026-10-28 - R21, see HE-26 / E-HE-59') and the Derelict Authoring writer (a one-line a_spine / DA-29 note). findings.section: Registry horror.state / horror.view / restore_codes and HE-37 frozen counter list (unresolved since 2026-10-28)
findings.finding: The registry `horror.state` entry still says `_RNG_COUNTER (trigger undefined, C-HE-30)` and its persisted list omits many HE-41 fields (reach_start_T, reach_smear_laid, strike_T, seats_hit, strike_hull_seg, goal_wp, goal_room, goal_commit_runs, dwell_start_T, held_at_leaf, transit_leg, ingress_seg, ingress_anchor_px, ingress_mark_T, smear_travel_px, chill_travel_px, the epoch ledgers, home_body_id, exo_source_class). data.summary: Fifth-pass design review of design/gdd/horror-entities.md (read-only, nothing edited). I found 0 BLOCKING defects: no defect makes implementation wrong or impossible at registry defaults. I found 18 RECOMMENDED items and 2 NICE. The tick, integer and probability figures I re-derived all hold. The receipt shows both the GDD and the registry changed since the 2026-10-28 entry, and the structure check shows all 8 sections present. Every Dependencies system has a GDD on disk. Only Depth Rings, Knowledge Codex and Co-op are undesigned, which is not a blocker under R9. The previous review had no blockers. The 2026-10-27 blockers (door_passage, AC-HE-88/130, the HE-41 manifest, the two-kernel epoch) are RESOLVED. Of the previous review's 16 recommended items, none is fully resolved and a few are partial. HE-26 now states the four-query eject budget, which is only partly closed. HE-11 now has a per-candidate hash term, but `anchor_local_key` and `run_n` are undefined and AC-HE-17 is stale. The items that matter most are: `horror_set_unfold_scale` with HOST origin (invalid under kernel CR-7, no settings surface, third pass); `threat_counter` naming and the AC-HE-136 gate, which can never clear; the two hold-stage definitions (sim 25 to 50 ticks, art 30 to 54); the zero-slack ingress relation against AC-HE-44; and the stale 'verbatim' neighbour quotes. The sibling-edit check found no breakage. One bidirectionality gap: Boarding and Derelict Authoring have not recorded the `a_spine` answer that Horror claims. Untestable ACs, with rewrites, are in the findings: AC-HE-106 ('five facings'), AC-HE-107 ('90 % of 5 judges'), Game Feel line 1 ('7 of 8, N >= 10') and AC-HE-120 ('checked by review'). Scope XL.
